title: [TransferEngine] Recover redis metadata connection after disconnects
body:
## Description

Fixes #4003.

`RedisStoragePlugin` in `mooncake-transfer-engine/src/transfer_metadata_plugin.cpp`
held a single long-lived `redisContext` and never rebuilt it. hiredis latches any
I/O error into the context and rejects every subsequent command, so **one
disconnect permanently disabled metadata publishing and lookup for the rest of the
process lifetime**: `get()` / `set()` / `remove()` returned false forever, segment
registration and lookup failed, and only restarting the process recovered.

We hit this in production with a managed Redis reached through a TCP load balancer
that reclaims connections idle for more than ~4000s. The connection is only touched
on segment (un)registration and on the first lookup of a given remote segment, so it
sits idle for hours; with no TCP keepalive nothing is sent during that window and the
load balancer silently reclaims the socket. Redis itself stayed healthy the whole
time — the broken state lived entirely in the client's cached context, so restarting
Redis did not help.

### What changed

1. **Reconnect and retry once on connection-level failure** (`execLocked`). Only null
   replies are retried: a `REDIS_REPLY_ERROR` means the server answered and rejected
   the command, so retrying cannot help. GET/SET/DEL are idempotent, so the retry is
   safe.
2. **AUTH/SELECT moved into the connect path** so they are replayed on every
   reconnect, and a construction-time failure is no longer terminal. Previously, a
   Redis that was unreachable at startup left `client_` null forever.
3. **Connect timeout, command timeout and TCP keepalive.** There was previously no
   timeout at all, so a slow or blackholed Redis could block the caller indefinitely
   while holding `access_client_mutex_`. The 3s values match the Redis client already
   used by Mooncake Store HA
   (`mooncake-store/src/ha/common/redis/redis_connection.cpp`). Keepalive matters
   because this connection is idle for long stretches, and the command timeout is what
   makes recovery work when a middlebox drops the flow without resetting it.
4. **`getWithStatus()` routed through the same retry path.** #3072 added that override
   so `syncSegmentCache()` can tell an absent key from a backend outage, but it issued
   its own `redisCommand()` with `if (!client_) return kUnavailable;` and no reconnect.
   Rebasing onto current main without touching it would have left #4003 reproducible
   through that entry point, and `syncSegmentCache()` calls it periodically. `get()` now
   delegates to it, which also removes the duplicated GET handling. A null reply after
   `execLocked()` means the backend is unreachable, so it maps to `kUnavailable` and
   never to `kNotFound`, preserving the invariant #3072 added.
5. **CI now executes the Redis regression tests.** The job that runs `ctest` configured
   the tree without `-DUSE_REDIS=ON`, so the suite was compiled but never run; the job
   that enables `USE_REDIS` builds without running `ctest`. Adding the flag is enough —
   `dependencies.sh` already installs `libhiredis-dev` on that runner and the top-level
   `CMakeLists.txt` calls `enable_testing()`.

No public interface changes. `MetadataStoragePlugin::Create()` could already return a
plugin with a dead connection, and no caller inspects connectivity, so behaviour for
callers is unchanged apart from now recovering.

One observable change for operators: `get()` now logs a nil reply at WARNING instead of
ERROR. An absent key is an expected outcome when resolving a segment that is not
registered yet, so the previous level reported a normal lookup miss as an error. The
message text is unchanged (`RedisStoragePlugin: unable to get <key> from <uri>`), so
anything matching on the text still matches, but alerting that keys on ERROR level will
no longer fire for lookup misses. The connection-level failure path — which is what
actually indicates a problem — is unaffected.

## Module

- [x] Transfer Engine (`mooncake-transfer-engine`)
- [ ] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)
- [ ] Reshard (`mooncake-reshard`)
- [ ] Mooncake EP (`mooncake-ep`)
- [ ] Mooncake PG (`mooncake-pg`)
- [ ] Integration (`mooncake-integration`)
- [ ] P2P Store (`mooncake-p2p-store`)
- [ ] Python Wheel (`mooncake-wheel`)
- [ ] Common (`mooncake-common`)
- [ ] Mooncake RL (`mooncake-rl`)
- [x] CI/CD
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Other

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other

## How Has This Been Tested?

Added `mooncake-transfer-engine/tests/transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test.cpp`, which
drives the plugin through the public `MetadataStoragePlugin::Create("redis://...")`
factory against an in-process RESP fake server. A real Redis cannot be scripted to
drop a connection at an exact moment, which is precisely the condition under test, and
the fake keeps the test hermetic (no Redis server required in CI).

Cases covered:

- set/get/remove round trip
- `set` recovers after the server drops the connection
- `get` recovers after the server drops the connection
- `getWithStatus` recovers after the server drops the connection
- `getWithStatus` reports `kNotFound` for an absent key while the server is up, and
  `kUnavailable` — never `kNotFound` — once the server is gone
- `remove` recovers after the server drops the connection
- recovery when Redis is unavailable at construction time and comes up later
- AUTH and SELECT are replayed on reconnect
- operations still fail, and fail fast, when Redis stays down

**Test commands:**
```bash
cmake -S mooncake-transfer-engine -B build -G Ninja \
  -DUSE_REDIS=ON -DUSE_HTTP=ON -DUSE_ETCD=OFF -DBUILD_UNIT_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build -j"$(nproc)" --target transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test
./build/tests/transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test

# and again under ASan + UBSan
cmake -S mooncake-transfer-engine -B build-asan -G Ninja \
  -DUSE_REDIS=ON -DUSE_HTTP=ON -DUSE_ETCD=OFF -DBUILD_UNIT_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g"
cmake --build build-asan -j"$(nproc)" --target transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test
./build-asan/tests/transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test
```

The binary is invoked directly above because `enable_testing()` is only called from the
top-level `CMakeLists.txt`, so a standalone Transfer Engine configure builds the test
target but registers no CTest tests. In CI the suite now runs through `ctest` from the
repository-root configure, because this PR adds `-DUSE_REDIS=ON` to the job that runs
it.

**Test results:**
- [x] Unit tests pass — 9/9, 167 ms total
- [ ] Integration tests pass (if applicable)
- [x] Manual testing done — see production validation below

```
[==========] Running 9 tests from 1 test suite.
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.SetGetRemoveRoundTrip (0 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.SetSucceedsAfterServerDropsConnection (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.GetSucceedsAfterServerDropsConnection (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.GetWithStatusRecoversAfterServerDropsConnection (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.GetWithStatusDistinguishesAbsentKeyFromOutage (20 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.RemoveSucceedsAfterServerDropsConnection (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.RecoversWhenRedisIsDownAtConstruction (20 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.AuthAndSelectAreReplayedOnReconnect (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.FailsWhenRedisStaysDown (20 ms)
[  PASSED  ] 9 tests.
```

The run emits the expected recovery diagnostics, e.g. `RedisStoragePlugin: SET
mooncake/node-1 failed on 127.0.0.1:17885: Server closed the connection;
reconnecting and retrying once`, followed by a successful retry.

The same 9 cases also pass under `-fsanitize=address,undefined` (190 ms, no
sanitizer reports and no LeakSanitizer findings at exit), which covers the
`redisContext` and `redisReply` lifetimes on the reconnect path.

These tests exercise the reconnect path via a peer that closes or refuses the
connection, so they cover the latched-error case rather than the silent-blackhole
case; the command timeout is therefore not exercised by them, which is also why the
whole suite finishes in 167 ms with no stalls.

**Production validation:** the reconnect, timeout and keepalive changes have been
cherry-picked onto v0.3.11.post1 and run for 5 days in a prefill/decode disaggregated
deployment on 8 H800 nodes, against the same managed Redis behind an L4 load balancer
described in #4003, where idle connections are reclaimed after roughly 4000s. Before the
patch the failure was fully deterministic there: SGLang (Store client) was restarted
roughly every 4 hours, and every restart reproduced it. The two intervals are different
things — the load balancer reclaims the connection about 4000s after the last Redis
access, but the dead context is only discovered at the next metadata operation, and a
restart is what forces those segment registrations and lookups to happen. Once
discovered, metadata publishing and lookup stayed broken for the remaining lifetime of
that process. After the patch the same restart cadence has not reproduced it once over
the 5-day run; a reclaimed connection now shows up only as a single warning followed by
a successful retry:

    RedisStoragePlugin: SET mooncake/ram/<segment> failed on <host>:6379: Server closed
    the connection; reconnecting and retrying once

To be precise about what that run covers: the deployed build predates `getWithStatus()`
(added by #3072), so the routing of that entry point through the same retry path is
covered by the unit tests above rather than by the production run.

CI coverage: the job that runs `ctest` previously configured without `-DUSE_REDIS=ON`,
so these tests were compiled but never executed. This PR adds the flag to that job, so
`transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test` now runs in CI. It needs no Redis server.

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have formatted my code using `./scripts/code_format.sh`
- [x] I have run pre-commit on the files changed in this PR and all hooks pass
- [ ] I have updated the documentation (if applicable) — no user-facing interface
      change; happy to document the timeout values if they should be configurable
- [x] I have added tests to prove my changes are effective
- [ ] For changes >500 LOC: I have filed an RFC issue — non-test changes are ~245
      lines in a single file and this is a bug fix rather than an architectural
      change, so no RFC was filed. Issue #4003 describes the bug.

### Known limitations, called out deliberately

- **No reconnect backoff.** While Redis is unreachable, every operation now attempts a
  fresh connection instead of failing immediately, and it does so while holding
  `access_client_mutex_`. Worst case for a blackholed Redis is roughly command timeout
  plus reconnect plus command timeout. This is still bounded, whereas before this PR
  the same situation could block forever with no timeout at all, but if maintainers
  prefer a cooldown (skip reconnect attempts for N ms after a failure) I am glad to
  add one.
- **SIGPIPE.** Writing to a socket the peer has closed can raise SIGPIPE on Linux, and
  no Mooncake code installs `SIG_IGN`. This exposure is unchanged by this PR — the
  pre-existing code issued the same write on the same dead socket — so it is not
  addressed here, but it seems worth a separate look.
- **`set`/`remove` do not inspect `reply->type`.** A server-level error such as
  `-READONLY` during a failover is still reported as success. This is pre-existing
  behaviour, left untouched to keep the diff focused, and tracked separately as
  requested.

AI assistance was used for code review, test scaffolding, and drafting this
description. The bug was diagnosed from a production incident on our side. I have
reviewed every changed line and can explain and defend the change end-to-end.

title: [1/3] [TransferEngine] Add HOST_NUMA Fabric allocation core
body:
## Summary

This PR provides the minimum Transfer Engine prerequisite for RFC #2914.

It adds CUDA `HOST_NUMA` Fabric allocation and closes the exact-range NVLink
registration lifecycle. It intentionally does **not** add the Store EGM pool or
the complete Provider/Consumer data path.

## Stack

This is **[1/3]** of the RFC implementation stack:

1. #2966 — HOST_NUMA/Fabric Transfer Engine prerequisite (this PR).
2. #3335 — Provider-owned EGM Store pool.
3. #3431 — direct remote-memory reads into GPU destinations.

The fork branches form this exact commit chain. GitHub still displays each
community PR against `main` because a cross-fork PR cannot use another fork
branch as its base.

## Core changes

### HOST_NUMA placement

- Adds `NvlinkHostNumaAllocation` for Fabric-capable CUDA `HOST_NUMA` memory.
- Validates the IPC switch and every visible GPU's VMM, Fabric, and HOST_NUMA
  VMM capabilities independently from NUMA discovery.
- Auto discovery sorts and deduplicates GPU-local NUMA IDs and validates each
  discovered node's granularity.
- Explicit placement validates only the selected node's granularity, so an
  unrelated node cannot block the override.
- Grants access to all visible GPUs in one batched `cuMemSetAccess` call.

### Retryable exact-range registration lifecycle

- Inserts a handle-free registration placeholder before retaining the CUDA
  allocation handle. A duplicate or map-allocation failure therefore cannot
  leave an untracked retained handle.
- If `cuMemRetainAllocationHandle()` fails, returns `ERR_MEMORY`, removes the
  placeholder, and does not publish metadata.
- Export failure, publication rollback, and public unregister share the same
  lock-held cleanup helper. A failed registration can be retried at the same
  address: pending cleanup finishes before a new handle is acquired, while a
  successful registration still rejects duplicates.
- Registration pins protect the allocation's VA throughout registration,
  rollback, and deferred/batch cleanup. `Release()` refuses to unmap a pinned
  range. A range being released remains unavailable for registration until
  address-free succeeds.
- Batch deletion retains handles and pins until metadata publication succeeds;
  partial cleanup retries skip already completed work.
- Metadata cleanup is recorded before external publication completes, so a
  later retry does not repeat a completed delete. `ERR_ADDRESS_NOT_REGISTERED`
  remains idempotent.
- A failed `cuMemRelease()` preserves the registration record and handle
  ownership; a later unregister retries only the remaining release stage.
- Allocation-owned release follows the same rule: ownership is cleared only
  after a successful release, and a failed call can be retried.
- Every rollback checks the release result instead of silently discarding it.
- `Create()` requires an empty output. An error may still return a partial
  owner; the caller must retain it and retry `Release()`. Destruction remains
  best-effort, not a replacement for successful explicit cleanup.

CUDA documents that these APIs may report errors from earlier asynchronous
work and does not explicitly guarantee failure atomicity. This PR deliberately
treats a non-successful release as retaining ownership so cleanup remains
retryable. That policy and its accepted ambiguity are documented in the code.
See the [CUDA Driver API virtual-memory documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.8.1/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__VA.html).

### Lifetime and tests

- Makes `OwnedRangeRegistry` a process-lifetime heap singleton to avoid static
  destruction-order hazards.
- Adds hardware-free scripted coverage for capability/placement failures,
  retain/export/publication failures, metadata retry, idempotent unregister,
  release retry, concurrent register/release, VA reuse, and partial batch cleanup.

### CI integration

- Runs the two fake-driver CTest entries in the existing `unit-tests` build
  with `USE_MNNVL=ON`, reusing the CUDA driver runtime setup.
- Removes the separate NVLink build and its path filter.
- Labels the real GPU entry `nvlink_gpu` and excludes only that entry from the
  CPU runner. Hardware and fake-driver cases use separate `GTEST_FILTER`
  environments, so they do not run twice.
- Adds an optional label exclusion to the shared CTest action. Nightly keeps
  its existing test selection when the input is omitted.

## Scope boundary

This PR does not change Store behavior, Consumer mapping/cache, wire schema,
`TransferMetadata` behavior, RDMA behavior, or Store configuration. Store EGM pooling,
the full Provider/Consumer path, and GB200/NVL72 integration validation belong
to the follow-up Store layer. GB200 validation is therefore not a merge gate
for #2966.

## Review size

- 1 logical commit.
- 12 changed files.
- +2,570/-2 lines.

## Validation

This revision consolidates the CI build and test selection; allocation,
registration, transfer, and cleanup behavior are unchanged.

- [x] clang-format 20 check on PR-changed C/C++ lines.
- [x] `git diff --check` and all applicable touched-file pre-commit hooks.
- [x] CUDA 12.8 ARM64 focused build.
- [x] `nvlink_vmm_unit` (2 tests).
- [x] CUDA-off Transfer Engine build.
- [x] CI shell-script regressions (12 tests, including 5 new CTest-action tests).
- [x] CTest JSON selection: only the real GPU entry is excluded; both
  fake-driver entries remain selected and ran successfully.
- [x] New-head complete `unit-tests` sweep and GitHub Actions CI Gate.

Local CUDA-on/off regression tests passed on the composed stack (#3431).
GitHub Actions passed the complete CTest sweep (226 entries) and CI Gate
for this revision. Both fake-driver entries ran successfully; the hardware-only
entry was excluded on the CPU runner.

Repository-wide `pre-commit run --all-files` is not a merge gate.

title: [Bugfix][TENT] Replace stale buffers when refreshing segment info
body:
## Description

Reusing a `SegmentInfo` output object with `getSegmentInfo()` appends new buffers to the previous result. Repeated queries duplicate entries, and a refresh after unregistering a buffer still reports that old address.

Clear the output buffer list after acquiring the current segment descriptor, before filling either the memory or file result. This is a one-line runtime fix. Add a regression to the existing local-memory lifecycle test that queries twice into one object, unregisters the buffer, and queries again.

This fixes output-object reuse, not the remote descriptor cache. The existing TENT CI job already runs this test target. No new state, configuration or test target is needed.

title: [TransferEngine] Reuse batch-local transport and single-device RDMA preparation
body:
## Description

#4259 already reuses the last-hit device inside one MR. The first-attempt
`selectDevice` / `selectPeerDevice` still runs for every request in a
submission, including the topology walk, even when the snapshot is a single
HCA with unique, non-overlapping coverage.

This change keeps a function-local cache for that first attempt. Consecutive
requests that stay inside the same buffer reuse `buffer_id` / `device_id`
without calling `selectDevice` again. The cache is not used on retries,
multi-HCA topology, overlapping range indexes, or `segments:` names.

#4273 already reuses `selectTransport` across consecutive same-`target_id`
requests. This PR also gates that reuse on `globalConfig().metacache`, so
`MC_DISABLE_METACACHE=1` still re-runs MultiTransport routing (protocol to
`Transport*`) on every request. It does not restore a per-request RDMA
`SegmentDesc` fetch; `submitTransferTask` still deduplicates by `target_id`.

Measured `submitTransfer` p50 on same-host H20 / `mlx5_bond_0` RDMA (classic
tebench, VRAM, GPU0→GPU1 READ, 4 KiB blocks). First two iterations skipped.
Wait / bandwidth is completion time and is not claimed. Baseline is current
`origin/main` (already includes #4259 and #4273). The cache is inactive on
multi-HCA topology, so these numbers apply to single-HCA hosts.

title: [Bugfix][Store] Preserve tenant in BatchReplicaClear RPC
body:
## Description

`MasterClient::BatchReplicaClear` previously omitted its configured tenant when invoking the RPC. The server wrapper therefore used the default tenant, which could silently leave the requested tenant's replicas untouched and clear same-named replicas in the default tenant instead.

This change:
- carries the client's tenant through the `BatchReplicaClear` RPC;
- resolves and validates that tenant in `WrappedMasterService` before forwarding to the existing tenant-aware service overload;
- preserves default-tenant behavior when tenant quotas are disabled; and
- adds an in-process RPC regression test with the same object key in two tenants.

title: [Bugfix][CI/Build] Reject ROCm wheels without multi-protocol routing
body:
## Description

Prevent ROCm release artifacts from silently shipping without the multi-protocol routing required for combined RDMA and HIP segments.

The published `mooncake-transfer-engine-rocm==0.3.13.post1` CPython 3.10 wheel was built from `v0.3.13.post1` (`719735896c86b56fabec6cf3e825fb2ea640597a`). Its release workflow enabled HIP but omitted `-DENABLE_MULTI_PROTOCOL=ON`, while that CMake option defaults to `OFF`. In a reported two-node MI355X test using `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x`, a cross-host GPU WRITE selected HIP IPC and failed with `hipIpcOpenMemHandle: invalid device context`. Rebuilding the same source with multi-protocol support enabled passed 16 bidirectional 2 MiB GPU WRITEs with full source and destination byte-integrity checks.

PR #3338 already corrected the current ROCm CI and release configuration to pass `-DENABLE_MULTI_PROTOCOL=ON`. This PR adds the missing artifact-level guard so a future workflow/configuration regression cannot publish another incorrectly configured ROCm wheel:

- expose `mooncake.engine.SUPPORT_MULTI_PROTOCOL` from the compiled extension;
- require ROCm wheel verification to reject an explicitly disabled capability;
- retain a narrow binary-marker fallback for workflow-dispatch backfills of older tags that predate the Python capability attribute;
- add positive and deliberately broken negative unit tests, including a chunk-boundary marker test.

Independent artifact inspection reproduced the build mismatch:

- affected PyPI CPython 3.10 wheel SHA-256: `4263d8a48c8bd05a340c19fa7533e012a3d4b9ac284161142a3062c24a4de4c6`; its `engine.so` lacks the multi-protocol-only `MC_DISABLE_HIP` marker and is rejected by this guard;
- current-main CI artifact from run `34701684601`, head `6ae74b3512c4d0ce70c4a7c22bc4f33aeb7d3ff8`, SHA-256 `084de7e711884f0fe9602ad0d5de0b46589526655e5a7c8b71ac8f53f616fe7a`; its `engine.so` contains the marker and is accepted.

This PR prevents recurrence but does not replace the immutable PyPI `0.3.13.post1` files. A new ROCm package version is still required to make the corrected build available through normal `pip install`.

Related: #3108, #3338. Open PR #3970 also edits the verifier, and #4177 moves the E2E verifier path; this change is intentionally narrow and may need to be carried across whichever layout lands first.

title: [Bugfix] Handle unavailable target segments in classic tebench
body:
## Description

Fixes #3979.

Classic `tebench` dereferenced a null segment descriptor when
`openSegment()` could not resolve a target. This caused the initiator to
terminate with `SIGSEGV` instead of reporting a startup failure.

This change validates the segment handle, descriptor, and registered buffer
list before starting worker threads. Invalid targets now produce a
target-specific error and `tebench` exits normally with a nonzero status.

The change does not alter transport selection, wire protocols, public APIs, or
benchmark result formats.

The regression test uses real Classic TCP engines and covers an unavailable
target, a target with no registered buffers, retry after a partial multi-target
failure, and a valid WRITE/READ path.

## Reproduction

Run a Classic initiator without starting the specified target:

```bash
MC_FORCE_TCP=1 ./build/issue-3979/mooncake-transfer-engine/benchmark/tebench \
  --backend=classic \
  --xport_type=tcp \
  --metadata_type=p2p \
  --target_seg_name=127.0.0.1:1 \
  --seg_type=DRAM \
  --total_buffer_size=65536
```

Before this change, the initiator terminates with `SIGSEGV`. After this change,
it logs `Failed to open target segment: 127.0.0.1:1` and exits normally with
status 1. See #3979 for the complete reproduction details.

title: [Doc][TENT] Add the deadline scheduling design doc
body:
## Description

Promised in the review of #3907: a design document for the deadline machinery, which until now had no entry of its own. Device selection is documented in `slice-spraying.md`; the admission queue and the RDMA bandwidth arbitration were mentioned only in passing inside its transmit-estimate section, and of the eleven `runtime_queue/*` keys one appeared anywhere in the docs.

`docs/source/design/tent/deadline-scheduling.md` covers, in order: the path a `deadline_ns` takes from `Request` to metric; the shared `DeadlineMlu` predictor and why the two layers read different `bytes_ahead`; the admission queue (capacity limits, EDF insert, slack promotion, deadline-infeasible drop, eligibility, dispatch window and the progress-worker fallback timer, the bandwidth provider); the RDMA arbitration (`orderByDeadline`, posted-bytes queue-ahead, slot-by-slot greedy order within a priority tier); the two bandwidth series and why per-completion timing cannot feed the predictors; a three-way comparison with device selection; every configuration key with type, default and meaning, plus the request fields and C++/Python examples; the two metrics; where each effect is observable (drop and arbitration act on RDMA only); and the known limits (no drop hook installed, no lower bound on the threshold, mixed-submit bypass, quarantined-owner bytes, no RDMA completion wake).

Two small edits alongside: `overview.md` gets a "TENT Deadline Scheduling" toctree entry, and `slice-spraying.md`'s transmit-estimate section links to the new page; one phrase there claimed the arbitration's 64 exactly-resolved slots are "more than one post can take", which is not so with the default `max_qp_wr` of 256, and is corrected. The `deadline_ns` comment in `types.h` still said the field "does not yet drive any admission or scheduling decision"; it now names what reads it and points at the document.

title: [Bugfix][Store] Read file-backed replicas in session API
body:
## Description

Fixes #3658.

After #3903, get sessions already support MEMORY (zero-copy) and DFS (staging + scatter). SSD-only / file-backed keys still failed session start with `702 INVALID_REPLICA` because `SelectSessionReplica` and the classify/execute pipeline only handled MEMORY and DFS.

This PR extends that same prepare → classify → execute pipeline (no separate packing layer):

1. **`SelectSessionReplica`**: after MEMORY / DFS, also accept a complete `LOCAL_DISK` or `DISK` replica. NOF-only keys still return `INVALID_REPLICA`.
2. **`classify_session_range_read_requests`**: route `LOCAL_DISK` → `local_disk_requests`, `DISK` → `disk_requests`.
3. **LOCAL_DISK** (`execute_session_local_disk_range_reads`): group by owner endpoint; restore each unique key once via shared `restore_offload_objects(..., allow_pinned=false)` (RPC into the owner's TE-registered client buffer — never the unregistered pinned arena); then `Client::BatchTransferReadOffloadRanges` from restored pointer + `src_offset` into already `register_buffer`'d destinations. The reader does **not** need a setup local buffer (`local_buffer_size=0` works). Same-node GPU destinations also go through TE (no offload `kLocalAddress` memcpy on the session path).
4. **DISK** (`execute_session_disk_range_reads`): one `Client::BatchGet` into a temp host buffer, then scatter by `src_offset`. Keys fail if the client has no allocator.
5. **Shared restore helper**: sequential `batch_get_into_offload_object_internal` now uses the same `restore_offload_objects` / `OffloadRestoreLease` (default `allow_pinned=true` so memcpy into the pinned arena remains available).

Duplicate keys restore once and scatter many times. Invalid ranges do not block valid entries. Lease is checked locally after transfer. Offload GC TTL rewrites only successful scatters to `OBJECT_HAS_LEASE`. No session-level object pin.

## Relation to #3903

#3903 landed the DFS session path and the shared pipeline. This branch was rebased onto main: redundant DFS / `MultiBufferRangeRequest` work from earlier revisions was dropped; only LOCAL_DISK / DISK session reads and the shared offload restore helper remain.

title: Store: add reusable ranged-read snapshots
body:
## Description

Add a reusable ranged-read metadata snapshot for Store reads and use it in the Engram and reconstructed-shard read paths.

The motivation is to reduce TTFT-sized Engram read latency by avoiding repeated Store query/lease metadata work when the same key set is read repeatedly. The actual TransferEngine/RDMA data path is unchanged in this PR.

### API and behavior

- Add `PyClient::RangedReadSnapshot`, a caller-owned snapshot of fresh `batch_query()` results.
- Add `prepare_get_into_ranges_snapshot(keys)` and `refresh_get_into_ranges_snapshot(...)`.
- Add `get_into_ranges_from_snapshot(...)` for reads that must use the supplied snapshot and must not re-query or renew leases.
- Cache one snapshot per `EngramStore` layer and invalidate it on `populate()` and successful `remove_from_store()`.
- Reuse the same snapshot abstraction in the parallel/reconstructed-shard read path when query results are already cached.

Snapshot refresh time is derived from the earliest lease timeout and is set to halfway through the remaining lease window. If any key fails query or has an expired lease, the snapshot is not treated as reusable. Ordinary `get_into_ranges` keeps the existing query-refresh behavior.

title: [Store] Read a batch's LOCAL_DISK endpoints in parallel
body:
## Description

We run SSD offload in production. A single batch's LOCAL_DISK replicas routinely
live on several offload endpoints rather than on one peer.

The client already groups such a batch by transport endpoint, but then reads the
groups one endpoint at a time:

```cpp
for (auto &[endpoint, objects] : offload_objects) {
    auto read_result = batch_get_into_offload_object_internal(endpoint, objects);
    ...
}
```

The groups are independent — different peers, different disks, different RPCs — so
the batch ends up waiting for the *sum* of the per-endpoint latencies instead of the
slowest one. Every extra peer a batch spans adds its full read to the total, and the
effect gets worse exactly as the cluster gets bigger. The client thread spends that
whole time blocked on `syncAwait`, not on CPU.

This PR reads the endpoints concurrently instead.

### Commits

**1. `[Store] Add ParallelExecute, a pool-backed bounded fan-out helper`**

`ParallelExecute(items, task, pool)` runs independent items on a persistent
`ThreadPool` the caller owns and returns one result per item **in input order**, so
the caller's existing merge loop needs no change at all. Design points worth a
comment:

- **All but the last item are dispatched; the last runs inline on the caller thread.**
  This keeps a single-item call off the pool entirely, and guarantees progress even
  when every worker is busy with something else.
- **A pool that cannot accept work degrades to serial execution** rather than
  failing — e.g. a pool already stopped during teardown. Correctness does not depend
  on the pool being alive.
- **A throwing task is reported as `INTERNAL_ERROR` for that item only.** Letting an
  exception escape a pool worker would terminate the process, and an unset promise
  would hang the caller forever in `future::get()`.
- **The pool is persistent by design.** The first consumer is the per-request read
  path, where creating threads per batch would cost more than the overlap saves.

This commit is self-contained and adds no caller; it compiles and tests on its own.

**2. `[Store] Read a batch's LOCAL_DISK endpoints in parallel`**

Three call sites shared that serial loop — `batch_get_buffer_internal`,
`batch_get_into_internal` and `batch_get_into_multi_buffers_internal`. The grouping
and the read now go through one private helper, `RealClient::read_local_disk_endpoints`,
which returns one entry per non-empty endpoint carrying that read's status. Each site
keeps its own merge loop unchanged.

**Only the reads move off the caller thread.** Checksum verification and every write
into the result vectors stay on the caller thread, after the join. The three merge
loops therefore need no concurrency reasoning, and the diff stays confined to how the
reads are issued.

On the reader being safe to call concurrently:

- `ClientRequester::invoke_rpc` enters through an atomic `RpcDrainGuard` and blocks on
  `syncAwait` while a separate io context pool drives the RPC.
- `Client::BatchGetOffloadObject` goes through `TransferSubmitter`, which
  `stress_workload_test` already drives from many threads.
- The pinned-arena local path shares `LoadBatch` with `FileStorage::BatchGet`, which
  coro_rpc handlers already call concurrently.

Worker count comes from `MC_OFFLOAD_PARALLEL_WORKERS`, default `8`. The workers spend
their time blocked on the peer RPC rather than on CPU, and the useful upper bound is
however many peers one batch spans.

**Two behavior notes, called out so they are not a surprise in review:**

- Endpoints with an empty batch are now skipped uniformly. Two of the three sites
  already did this; the third cannot produce one, since it emplaces a key immediately
  after `try_emplace` on the endpoint.
- The failure log in `batch_get_into_internal` now names the endpoint, which the log
  order no longer implies once the reads overlap.

**3. `[Doc] Document MC_OFFLOAD_PARALLEL_WORKERS in the SSD offload guide`**

A row in the core settings table plus a short note on what the workers block on.

### Limitations / non-goals

- **A batch confined to a single endpoint gains nothing** — it takes the inline path
  and never touches the pool. The win scales with how many peers a batch spans.
- **No change to error semantics.** Per-endpoint failures land on exactly the same
  keys as before.
- The pool is per `RealClient` and sized once at construction; it is not resized at
  runtime.

Non-test, non-config code is roughly 290 lines, so no RFC issue was filed.

title: [Store] Self-heal dangling LOCAL_DISK replicas on the read path
body:
## Description

A COMPLETE LOCAL_DISK replica whose backing file physically disappears (manual wipe, RemoveAll broadcast, disk loss) stays registered forever, and every `batch_get` against it just logs "SSD read failed" and hands back an empty buffer. #3711 already self-heals exactly this on the Put path (probe file existence, `EvictDiskReplica`, clean retry); the read path had no equivalent, which is the still-open half of #3465 and what #3884 tracks.

On a failed SSD read in `batch_get_buffer_internal`, the same heal now runs: the offload-file probe proves the backing file gone, the dangling replica is evicted master-side via `EvictDiskReplica`, and the key is retried once so a surviving replica (or a fresh re-put) can serve it instead of returning empty. When nothing survives, the master stops advertising the key and the miss surfaces honestly. The retry only ever heals distinct dead replicas, so it terminates. Checksum failures keep their existing path (the file exists, just corrupt, so no heal fires). Healthy reads are untouched; this is failure-path only.

`healDanglingLocalDiskReplica` moves from private to public in `client_service.h` so the RealClient read path can share the exact Put-side logic instead of growing a second copy.

Refs #3884, #3465, #3711.

title: [Store] Add immutable bucket allocator for DFS replicas
body:
## Description

This PR implements the DFS immutable Bucket allocator proposed in:

- RFC: https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/3641

It introduces a pluggable `GlobalAllocatorInterface` for DFS replica allocation while preserving the existing `DfsGlobalAllocator` as the default `shard` implementation.

A new `ImmutableBucketAllocator` can be selected with:

```bash
MOONCAKE_DFS_ALLOCATOR=bucket
```

The Bucket allocator stores objects as aligned, append-only immutable entries in fixed-capacity Bucket files. Buckets are created on demand and reclaimed in LRU order.

The existing `DistributedFSDescriptor` wire format is unchanged. In Bucket mode, the existing `shard_idx` field carries the Bucket ID, preserving serialization compatibility.

### Main changes

#### Pluggable DFS allocator

- Extract `GlobalAllocatorInterface` as the Master-facing DFS allocation contract.
- Adapt `DfsGlobalAllocator` to implement the interface.
- Keep `shard` as the default allocator with unchanged behavior.
- Add configuration parsing and validation for `shard` and `bucket`.

#### Immutable Bucket allocation

- Create fixed-capacity Bucket files on demand.
- Store values as aligned, append-only entries:

  ```text
  [value bytes][zero alignment padding]
  ```

- Track entries through `PENDING`, `COMMITTED`, and `TOMBSTONE` states.
- Never overwrite entries or reuse tombstoned or rolled-back ranges.
- Assign monotonically increasing Bucket IDs.
- Allow ordered batch allocation across multiple Buckets.
- Roll back all reservations if any allocation in a batch fails.
- Match complete descriptors when committing, freeing, or updating entries.
- Seal full Buckets and create new ones up to the configured limit.

#### Bucket-level LRU eviction

- Track access and reclaim complete Buckets in LRU order.
- Exclude the active Bucket and Buckets containing pending or protected entries.
- Lock affected metadata shards in a stable order and validate every live entry against its exact DFS descriptor.
- Abort the entire eviction if any entry is processing, leased, pinned, or otherwise invalid.
- Remove replicas from metadata before deleting the Bucket file. Failed file deletion keeps the Bucket charged against capacity for a later retry.
- Trigger reclamation at configured watermarks and when allocation is exhausted.

#### Synchronous buffered Bucket I/O

- Extend the filesystem adapter to open existing files without creating them.
- Use synchronous buffered positional I/O with short-lived descriptors for Bucket requests, while retaining cached descriptors for shard files.
- Handle interrupted and partial POSIX operations, treating zero progress, premature EOF, and incomplete transfers as errors.
- Validate Bucket paths, IDs, descriptor alignment, object sizes, and ranges before I/O.
- Never create a file implicitly for an invalid or missing Bucket descriptor.

#### Master and Client integration

- Select the configured allocator during Master initialization and allocate DFS replicas through the common interface.
- Keep Bucket entries pending while replicas are `PROCESSING`, then commit them in `PutEnd` before publication.
- Tombstone reservations when writes are revoked, removed, or replaced.
- Keep DFS writes synchronous and revoke failed writes so incomplete data is never published.
- Attempt one validated whole-Bucket eviction when Bucket capacity is exhausted.
- Preserve existing shard expansion and eviction behavior in `shard` mode.

#### Configuration

The following settings are introduced:

```bash
MOONCAKE_DFS_ALLOCATOR=shard | bucket
MOONCAKE_DFS_BUCKET_CAPACITY=1073741824
MOONCAKE_DFS_MAX_BUCKET_COUNT=64
```

The existing DFS settings continue to configure common filesystem and eviction behavior:

```bash
MOONCAKE_DFS_ROOT_DIR
MOONCAKE_DFS_FS_ADAPTER
MOONCAKE_DFS_ALIGNMENT
MOONCAKE_DFS_EVICTION_ENABLED
MOONCAKE_DFS_EVICTION_HIGH_WATERMARK
MOONCAKE_DFS_EVICTION_LOW_WATERMARK
MOONCAKE_DFS_EVICTION_CHECK_INTERVAL
```

`MOONCAKE_DFS_BUCKET_CAPACITY` must be nonzero, aligned to `MOONCAKE_DFS_ALIGNMENT`, and representable by the filesystem interface. `MOONCAKE_DFS_MAX_BUCKET_COUNT` must be positive.

#### Documentation

- Document the immutable Bucket layout and lifecycle.
- Document allocator selection and Bucket-specific environment variables.
- Describe allocation, rollback, commit, and whole-Bucket eviction.
- Document current operational and recovery limitations.

### Compatibility

- `shard` remains the default allocator with unchanged allocation, eviction, and I/O behavior.
- `DistributedFSDescriptor` serialization remains unchanged, so existing clients can continue using shard descriptors without configuration changes.
- Bucket capacity settings affect only `bucket` mode.
- Shard count and capacity settings do not control Bucket allocation.

title: [TransferEngine] Recover partial memory unregisters
body:
## Summary

Fix multi-transport memory unregister retries that can otherwise leave a buffer permanently blocked after one transport succeeds and another returns a transient error.

Fixes #4240

## Root cause

The Transfer Engine retained only the top-level memory region. It did not retain which transport instances had registered that address or which unregister operations had already completed. Retrying every transport caused an already-completed transport to return `ERR_ADDRESS_NOT_REGISTERED`, which could permanently mask recovery of the transport that originally failed.

The same address state is shared by scalar, batch, multi-protocol, and shared-memory lifecycle paths. Those paths also need consistent reservation and fail-closed behavior when cleanup cannot be proven complete.

## Design

- Record the transport instances that actually registered each address.
- Persist explicit unregister successes and retry only unfinished `(address, transport)` pairs.
- Keep transport errors fail-closed; `ERR_ADDRESS_NOT_REGISTERED` is not reinterpreted as successful cleanup for a previously registered transport.
- Serialize overlapping registration and unregister operations with full-range reservations.
- Keep the reservation through physical shared-memory release.
- Preserve native batch transport calls while grouping tracked addresses only by transports that registered them and have not already completed.
- Process untracked batch addresses separately so their errors cannot poison successfully cleaned tracked addresses.
- Quarantine addresses when registration rollback or an aggregate tracked batch result cannot prove cleanup completed. Quarantined ranges remain unavailable for the lifetime of the engine rather than being unsafely reused.
- Reject duplicate addresses within one multi-protocol transport before any side effect.
- Validate SHM ranges while holding the allocation lock, establish the engine reservation before releasing that lock, and only then invoke transports. This prevents an invalid SHM range from being quarantined and closes the concurrent free window for scalar, batch, and multi-protocol registration, including TCP-only registration of SHM-backed memory.

## Regression coverage

The hardware-free unit coverage exercises:

- scalar partial failure followed by successful retry and address reuse;
- genuine and partial-cleanup failures remaining fail-closed;
- missing-address compatibility and error precedence;
- batch transport selection, completed-transport skipping, and ambiguous-failure quarantine;
- scalar, batch, and multi-protocol registration rollback failures;
- duplicate multi-protocol registrations;
- register/unregister races, including interior-address overlap;
- shared-memory release reservation cleanup;
- SHM sub-range rejection followed by successful scalar, batch, SHM-only MP, and TCP-only MP retries, with explicit checks that failed validation leaves no metadata.

The Linux unit-test job now enables `ENABLE_MULTI_PROTOCOL`, so the multi-protocol regressions are compiled and executed by the PR gate.

## Validation

Passed locally:

- clang-format 20.1.8
- all applicable pre-commit hooks for the changed files
- YAML validation
- codespell
- `git diff --check`
- merge-tree check against current upstream `main`

The local macOS host does not provide the project's Linux `numa` and `ibverbs` dependency environment, so the C++ target could not be built locally. The upstream Linux matrix is the authoritative compile and runtime validation for this head.

The previous head completed compilation and ran 220 CTest targets. Its only test failure was `ShmTransportE2E.RegisterSubRangeFails`: a side-effect-free SHM validation error was incorrectly treated as an ambiguous rollback and quarantined the address. This head fixes that path with lock-bound prevalidation and adds scalar, batch, SHM-only MP, and TCP-only MP coverage. The two other failed jobs in that run stopped while downloading sccache from GitHub with HTTP 504 responses and did not reach compilation.

## Risk

The main compatibility change is that conflicting lifecycle operations now fail with `ERR_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` instead of racing. Ambiguous rollback and aggregate batch failures quarantine affected tracked ranges for the engine lifetime. This intentionally favors memory safety over address reuse when the transport contract cannot prove that hardware and metadata cleanup both completed.

title: [TransferEngine] Skip in-flight task walk in getBatchTransferStatus for RDMA
body:
## Description

`getBatchTransferStatus()` currently walks every task on every in-flight poll. For large RDMA batches that is O(task) CPU on the wait path, even though CQ completions already know how many tasks have finished.

This PR:

1. Always publishes `BatchDesc::finished_task_count` from `Slice::markSuccess` / `markFailed` (no `USE_EVENT_DRIVEN_COMPLETION` required). Each CQ completion does a second `lock xadd` on `completion_state` (handshake) in addition to `success_slice_count` / `failed_slice_count` (poll). Those fields are laid out on one cacheline so the extra RMW does not bounce a second line. Packing the two counters into one word is a follow-up; it would touch every transport's `getTransferStatus`.
2. Marks a batch `counter_eligible` only when every submitted transport opts in via `supportsBatchCompletionCounter()`. RDMA opts in. TCP, NVLink, and mixed batches stay on the walk **by design**: their progress is driven by `getTransferStatus()` (NVLink `cudaStreamQuery`, TCP polling), so they are not expected to join the counter later.
3. Seals each RDMA task after `submitTransferTask()` so a CQ completion that races submit cannot publish the task until its slice list is complete. Seal and last-slice CQ share one packed `completion_state` word (bit 63 = sealed, low bits = completed slices), so they cannot miss each other. Handshake / dummy slices with `batch_id == 0` do not touch `BatchDesc`. Unseal stores 0 with `RELEASE`. Non-EDC CQ does not write `is_finished`; `getTransferStatus` on the COMPLETED walk still does, so `freeBatchID` after a polled COMPLETED is unchanged. EDC still writes `is_finished` from CQ so a CV waiter can `freeBatchID` without that walk.
4. Lets in-flight `getBatchTransferStatus()` return `WAITING` from the counter when `counter_eligible && slice_timeout <= 0 && !has_failure && finished < task_count`.
5. On that fast path, `status.transferred_bytes` stays 0 while `WAITING`. That is still a valid lower bound; the accurate total is filled in when the batch reaches `COMPLETED`. Documented in the C++ API.

On completion (or timeout / failure / mixed transport) the existing per-task walk still runs once to aggregate bytes and surface errors. `mp_submitTransfer` keeps the old poll path. `MC_SLICE_TIMEOUT > 0` still walks (an O(1) timeout check is a follow-up).

### Classic tebench A/B (busy-wait; not a speedup claim)

H20, `mlx5_bond_0` loopback, DRAM READ, 4096 B, 1 thread, 5 s.
Same #4193 `getBatchTransferStatus` wait; engine only (`origin/main` walk vs this PR).
Skip first 2 iterations. Do not treat classic tebench BW as the success metric.

| batch | engine | submit p50 | wait p50 | polls/wait p50 | BW (GB/s) |
|------:|--------|-----------:|---------:|---------------:|----------:|
| 4096 | walk | 2683 µs (2643–2756) | 2392 µs (2137–2616) | 57 | 2.63 |
| 4096 | this PR | 2706 µs (2646–2754) | 2294 µs (2182–2647) | 71873 | 2.71 |
| 207360 | walk | 68.6 ms (67.2–69.3) | 779 ms (498–897) | 418 | 1.01 |
| 207360 | this PR | 73.8 ms (72.8–73.9) | 1111 ms (851–1217) | 5.4e7 | 0.76 |

n after warmup: 4096 ≈ 940–970; 207360 is 6 vs 4 (5 s wall).

| batch | submit | wait | what it shows |
|------:|--------|------|----------------|
| 4096 | unchanged | ranges overlap; not a −4% win | poll is now O(1) (57 → 7e4); wall already ~RDMA (~2.3 ms) |
| 207360 | +5.2 ms, ranges disjoint: per-task seal, not noise | worse (poll storm) | cheaper poll ≠ cheaper wait on an un-yielded loop. Batch-level seal was 71.16 vs 71.14 ms submit; not in this PR |

In-flight poll is O(1) instead of O(task). That does not shorten a waiter that never yields. A waiter that sleeps or waits on a CV between polls (Store EDC) can use it; classic tebench does not.

title: [Store] Track requested and reserved allocation sizes without changing wire formats
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4222/files) against `main`.

## Description

Related to #3808 (E01). This is the **runtime accounting-fields slice**: an
`AllocatedBuffer` now distinguishes the caller's requested byte count from the
extent its allocator actually reserved, for both the CacheLib and
OffsetAllocator backends.

E01 in the roadmap reads "Distinguish requested bytes from allocator-reserved
bytes while keeping old descriptors readable". This patch does that at runtime
and keeps old descriptors readable by rebuilding the extent from real backend
metadata after a restore. It deliberately **adds no field to any writer**, so it
does not claim completion of a persisted descriptor schema extension. If a
persisted field is what E01 is meant to require, that is a separate wire
contract and this patch is its prerequisite, not its substitute.

What changes:

- `AllocatedBuffer::requested_size()` names the existing `size()` value;
  `size()` keeps its meaning as the transfer length for the descriptor and the
  requested-based usage counters.
- `AllocatedBuffer::reserved_size()` returns `std::optional<std::size_t>`.
  `nullopt` means "no physical allocation has been reconstructed yet" — never
  zero, never `requested_size()`.
- The owning constructor now takes `reserved_size` as a **required** parameter,
  so every production allocation site had to state where its value comes from.
  All five sites were audited: CacheLib fresh allocate, CacheLib import, Offset
  fresh allocate, Offset import, and the descriptor rebinding in
  `Serializer<AllocatedBuffer>::deserialize`.
- CacheLib reads the allocation class size from the chunk's own slab header
  (`MemoryAllocator::getAllocInfo(...).allocSize`), for fresh allocations and for
  `importAllocations` alike. `padding_size = max(requested, kMinSliceSize)` is
  only the allocation *input*; class rounding can reserve more, so it is no
  longer treated as the extent.
- OffsetAllocator reads the real node extent (`node.dataSize <<
  multiplier_bits`) while the allocation lock is already held and carries it on
  the handle. `createHandleAtNode` and the new bounds-checked
  `allocationReservedSize()` read the same source, so a handle rebuilt from
  persisted state reports the extent it was actually allocated with instead of
  re-deriving it from the current rounding rules. `OFFSET_ALLOCATOR_NOT_ROUND_UP`
  and legacy size classes therefore stay correct.
- Both backends **enforce** `reserved_size() >= requested_size()`. An extent that
  is missing or smaller than the request rolls the allocation back (the raw chunk
  is freed / the node released), records no usage, and fails the call. `nullopt`
  is consequently reachable only for buffers that own no physical allocation —
  it is not a silent fallback for a failed lookup.
- `ImportCachelibBufferAllocator` resolves every extent **before** the first
  `adoptImportedBuffer` call records usage, so a partially adopted import cannot
  publish accounting.
- `AllocatedBuffer` move construction/assignment were declared in the header but
  never defined, so no object-level move existed. They are now defined so the new
  field follows ownership: the destination releases its previous allocation
  exactly once, self-assignment is an explicit no-op, and the moved-from object
  owns nothing. `SegmentLifetime::isAvailable()` also treats a moved-out token as
  unavailable instead of dereferencing a null pointer.

**This changes two public constructor signatures** (`AllocatedBuffer` and
`OffsetAllocationHandle` gained a required parameter), which is a source-level
breaking change for any out-of-tree caller. In-tree call sites are updated,
including the test double in `tests/test_buffer_allocator.h`.

Requested-based accounting is untouched: `RecordAllocation`,
`RecordDeallocation`, `SetUsageBytesForRestore` and `GetUsageBytes` still operate
on requested bytes, and `deallocate` still frees the whole chunk/node and
decrements by `size()`.

## Module

- [x] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Breaking change

## How Has This Been Tested?

**Test commands:**
```bash
# Focused suites, both revisions (base 2abe68b0 and the patched tree)
ctest --test-dir <build> --output-on-failure --no-tests=error -R \
  '^(buffer_allocator_test|offset_allocator_test|serializer_test|replica_allocator_test|segment_pool_test|master_metrics_test|master_snapshot_codec_test|store_resource_snapshot_codec_test)$'

# New E01 cases only
build/mooncake-store/tests/buffer_allocator_test --gtest_filter='*E01*'
build/mooncake-store/tests/offset_allocator_test  --gtest_filter='*E01*'

# Store-path integration suites, both revisions
build/mooncake-store/tests/master_service/dsl/master_scenario_test
build/mooncake-store/tests/dummy_client_get_buffer_test

# Sanitizers (repo-supported option + UBSan), separate build directory
cmake -S . -B build-asan -DENABLE_ASAN=ON -DBUILD_UNIT_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all" \
  -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-fsanitize=undefined"
ctest --test-dir build-asan -R '^(buffer_allocator_test|offset_allocator_test)$'
```

**Test results:**
- [x] Unit tests pass
- [x] Integration tests pass (if applicable)
- [x] Manual testing done (describe below)

Environment: Ubuntu 22.04.5, g++ 11.4.0, CMake 3.27.0, `Unix Makefiles`,
`RelWithDebInfo`. Host-side work; no GPU used. Base SHA
`2abe68b0f89238cda206bdb41d71ab6fc52f6469` (upstream/main at the time of the
work — upstream has since advanced).

| Check | Base | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Focused suites (8 targets) | 8/8 pass | 8/8 pass |
| `master_scenario_test` | 44/44 pass | 44/44 pass |
| `dummy_client_get_buffer_test` | 12 pass, 2 skipped | 12 pass, 2 skipped |
| ASan + Leak + UBSan (`buffer_allocator_test`, `offset_allocator_test`) | — | 34 and 61 tests pass, no sanitizer report |

18 new cases are added (13 in `buffer_allocator_test`, 5 in
`offset_allocator_test`) covering per-backend reserved extents against
**independent** oracles (the configured CacheLib allocation-class set; the
OffsetAllocator free-space delta — never the same helper that produced the
value), move and self-move, import with holes, restored-handle extent, CXL offset
handling, concurrency, failure paths and zero-length behaviour. Zero-length
behaviour was additionally measured with a probe binary built against both
revisions: identical output.

**Cross-version wire compatibility.** A fixture tool was compiled against both
revisions with identical flags and link line, so the two binaries differ only by
this patch. It emits the exact `Serializer<AllocatedBuffer>` bytes and reads them
back:

- `base emit` and `patched emit` are **byte-identical** (same sha256).
- old→old, **old→new**, new→new and **new→old** all pass with 0 failures over
  `requested = {477, 4097, 100000}` on an OFFSET and a CACHELIB region.
- The patched reader reconstructs, with no persisted field at all:
  OFFSET `477 → 480`, `4097 → 4608`, `100000 → 106496`;
  CACHELIB `477 → 480`, `4097 → 4544`, `100000 → 103496`. The two backends
  legitimately disagree for the same request, which is precisely why each must
  report its own metadata.
- Wire shape is asserted directly: every buffer record is a 5-element array and
  every offset record's nested handle is a 3-element array.

**Performance.** The expected cost is one extra metadata read per allocation (a
slab-header read for CacheLib, one node read under the already-held lock for
Offset), against 250.8–299.9 ns/op measured at one thread. A paired 72-arm
fresh-process screen could not resolve it and is reported as inconclusive: the
A/A control, which runs the *same baseline binary in both arms*, reported a
nominally significant **+11.72 %** (95 % interval [+0.72, +23.93]), and every
A/P interval crossed zero. No performance claim is made in either direction; a
verdict needs a quiet, dedicated machine with clock/power stabilisation.

**Object size:** `AllocatedBuffer` 176 → 208 B and `OffsetAllocationHandle`
40 → 56 B (`std::optional` fields). This is per live replica, not per segment.

**Not tested:** real CXL / NoF device I/O (no hardware; the address-representation
half is covered by a metadata-level test that confirms a CXL offset is *not*
attributed to slab metadata), and real-etcd HA restore E2E.

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [ ] I have formatted my code using `./scripts/code_format.sh`
- [ ] I have run pre-commit on the files changed in this PR and all hooks pass
- [ ] I have updated the documentation (if applicable)
- [x] I have added tests to prove my changes are effective
- [ ] For changes >500 LOC: I have filed an RFC issue

Notes on the unticked boxes, so nothing is implied that was not done:

- **`code_format.sh`**: the script hard-requires clang-format 20, which is not
  available on the host used for this work. Instead `git clang-format-14 --diff`
  was applied to the changed lines only; 20 format hunks were fixed and 0 remain.
  Whole-file formatting was deliberately avoided because clang-format 14 also
  disagrees with the committed style in untouched regions. A maintainer run of
  `scripts/code_format.sh` is the authority.
- **pre-commit**: not installed on the host. `git diff --check` is clean and the
  changed files end with a newline, which is what the local hooks would assert.
- **documentation**: no user-facing documentation describes allocation
  accounting, so there is nothing to update; the semantics are documented in the
  new API comments.
- **RFC**: no separate RFC was filed. The work is tracked by the E01 item in
  #3808, and this PR proposes the runtime-first scope boundary explicitly rather
  than assuming it.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

- [ ] No AI tools were used
- [x] AI tools were used (specify below)

AI tools assisted with drafting the implementation, the tests, and the
measurement/evidence harness (paired A/B screening, the cross-revision wire
fixture tool, and the sanitizer runs). All results in this description were
produced by commands run on the target host, and the human submitter has
reviewed the change and is responsible for understanding and defending it.

Test and benchmark sources are retained locally; the validation results below refer to those local files.

title: [TransferEngine] Add native RDMA notifications
body:
## Description

Classic TE sends notifications over TCP even when data transfers use ordinary RDMA. This adds a synchronous TCP round trip to transfers that request notifications.

This PR adds native SEND/RECV notifications to ordinary `RdmaTransport`:

- Add one notification QP per endpoint and exchange its connection information through the existing endpoint handshake.
- Share a notification CQ within each context, with capacity management and generation-based completion routing.
- Manage notification buffers, backpressure, reconnection, and teardown within the endpoint lifecycle.
- Reuse `MC_RDMA_NOTIFY_ENABLED` and `MC_RDMA_NOTIFY_OOB_FALLBACK`, without adding configuration variables or changing `rdma_twosided`.

A successful native notification send indicates local submission, not confirmed remote receipt. Unsupported peers and oversized messages may fall back to TCP when enabled; failed or uncertain sends are not replayed.

Each endpoint uses 32 MiB of registered host memory for notification buffers. The maximum combined `name` and `msg` size is 65,528 bytes.

## Module


title: [Store] Add P01 codec evidence and real-etcd replay checks
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4160/files) against `main`.

## Description

Implements the **P01 codec evidence experiment** in #3808 without changing production persistence or writer selection.

**Depends on #4141 (W02), pinned to `e92af584fa106668c3e311b66e1592bd8922b42b`.** This is a separate dependent branch, not an addition to the W02 PR. Until W02 merges, this draft's main-based diff includes its two prerequisite commits; the P01-specific commit adds only `benchmarks/oplog_codec/`. Rebase/drop those prerequisites after #4141 merges.

- Compare production JsonCpp JSON, a same-library nlohmann JSON/base64 control, CBOR, and MessagePack using production batch validators/checksums.
- Add six opaque-payload profiles and five generated production-schema profiles with actual struct_pack metadata/Segment serialization.
- Exercise the latest asynchronous durable awaiter through production writer/storage and a test-only backend bridge on isolated real etcd namespaces.
- Restart etcd, audit every acknowledged operation, replay through production OpLogApplier/StandbyMetadataStore, and check fencing/corruption and duplicate replay.
- Publish two complete raw measurement passes, summaries, environment/hash metadata, and the eight-case E2E report under `benchmarks/oplog_codec/results/2026-09-16/`.

Generated-schema payload sizes shrink approximately 24–26%. Final-pass observed CPU ratios versus the same-library control span 3.00–14.36× encode and 1.37–3.57× decode. These are shared-host codec microbenchmarks with substantial variability, **not service-throughput gains or a CBOR/MessagePack selection**. The test bridge's transcoding overhead is not timed. RPC/HA promotion/resource rebuilding is outside scope; P02/P03 remain conditional.

This is benchmark/test-only work covered by the P01 roadmap, not a >500 LOC production architectural change. Kept draft for the W02 dependency and human review.

## Module

- [x] Other: standalone benchmark and recorded evidence

title: [Store] Add a dual-format OpLog batch reader (JSON + framed binary)
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4194/files) against `main`.

## Summary

P02 reader half of the batch-OpLog format migration. The production writer is
unchanged: it still emits the existing JSON batch record, and this PR adds no
writer selector, no environment variable, no default switch and no history
migration.

What it does:

- adds **one** format/version dispatch point at the existing
  `DecodeOpLogBatchRecord` entry, whose signature is unchanged. A complete
  binary magic selects the binary decoder, a non-empty truncation of the magic
  is its own error, and every other input goes to the **unchanged JSON reader
  exactly once** (no `try A then B` fallback chain), so the historical
  whitespace/BOM/parser acceptance domain, base64 canonicality checks and error
  strings do not change;
- adds a single binary encoding (MessagePack body inside a fixed 16-byte
  envelope) decoded by a bounded reader written for this six-element schema
  only: declared lengths are checked against the remaining bytes and the field
  budgets before any allocation, only unsigned integer encodings are accepted,
  `payload` must be `BIN` (STR/EXT rejected, including extension subtypes),
  `op_type` is range-checked before narrowing, and the whole body must be
  consumed;
- verifies the **existing canonical logical batch checksum**, so both physical
  encodings of the same logical batch agree on the checksum value. This
  deliberately does not change the JSON checksum algorithm, the JSON writer
  output, the durable prefix encoding or the snapshot encodings. A consequence
  worth stating: this version therefore does **not** remove the base64/JSON
  projection cost, so the P01 decode-speed multiples do not carry over to it;
- keeps failure atomic: validation happens on local candidates and the caller's
  record is assigned exactly once on success, so a failed decode cannot expose
  half a batch.

Startup prefix validation, the writer's ambiguous-transaction readback and the
batch auditor inherit the capability through the shared entry point with no
further edits.

## Testing

Executed on Ubuntu 22.04 / gcc 11.4.0 (RelWithDebInfo, `USE_CUDA=OFF`,
`WITH_EP=OFF`).

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `oplog_batch_dual_codec_test` (new, 34 cases) | pass |
| `oplog_batch_codec_test` | 32 pass |
| `oplog_batch_storage_test` (+8 new mixed-format cases) | 64 pass |
| `oplog_batch_standby_reader_test` | 26 pass |
| `oplog_applier_test` | 28 pass |
| `ordered_oplog_writer_test` | 50 pass |
| `oplog_batch_auditor_test` | 8 pass |

CTest registration was verified before running, so an empty pattern cannot look
like a pass: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 7`.

The new suite covers every valid `OpType`; byte-exact payload/key preservation
including all 256 byte values, embedded NUL and non-UTF-8 keys; every truncation
point of a valid record; header field corruption, trailing bytes and a
concatenated second body; strict type rejection (signed ints, float, bool, nil,
maps, payload as STR, payload as EXT, out-of-range `op_type` without narrowing);
sequence/range/checksum rejection including single-bit flips; forged
`bin32`/`array32` lengths failing without large allocation; and fixed-seed
property tests (1000 constrained batches round-trip and agree with the JSON
reader). The JSON writer output for four fixtures is asserted byte-for-byte
against bytes captured from a pristine pre-change build.

Separately built with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all`:
7/7 suites pass, 0 sanitizer findings. `libFuzzer` was not run.

A real-etcd 3.3.25 integration harness (producer in one process, etcd restart,
reader in a fresh process) confirms the all-JSON control replays end to end and
that the unchanged writer appends JSON after the terminal batch; five
corrupt-history scenarios fail closed.

## Known blocker (not fixed here)

The production etcd **Range** read path is not binary-transparent: the Go bridge
marshals range results through `encoding/json`, which rewrites every byte
`>= 0x80` to U+FFFD. A controlled probe shows a 256-byte value returning as 512
bytes from `Range` while `Get` is byte-exact. So `ReadBatch` (single key) reads a
framed binary batch correctly end to end, while `ReadBatchesAfter` cannot deliver
binary bytes, which means range-based replay of binary history cannot succeed
yet.

This is pre-existing infrastructure behaviour and outside the reader diff, but
it must be resolved before any binary writer can ship. Options: hex/base64 the
range response, return lengths plus raw pointers, or read the replay range by
key. Happy to take whichever direction maintainers prefer.

## Open gates

- Maintainer approval of the physical codec, the envelope, and the
  checksum-reuse decision. The magic, `codec_id`, envelope version and the
  checksum choice are **local proposals**, not project-assigned values.
- The etcd Range bridge fix above.

Related: #3808 (HA/OpLog roadmap), #4141 (W02, merged), #4160 (P01 evidence,
open). Built on top of the W02 work already in `main`; it does not duplicate it
and does not implement P03.

## Checklist

- [x] JSON writer output byte-for-byte unchanged (verified against a pristine
      baseline build and pinned by an in-tree golden test)
- [x] Durable prefix / producer view / snapshot encodings untouched
- [x] Exactly one new binary codec; format identification is deterministic
- [x] Payload and string bytes preserved; numeric range, unknown version,
      checksum and shape validated
- [x] Failed decode leaves the caller's record unchanged
- [x] Oversized/forged-length input fails closed
- [x] No writer selector, no P03, no descriptor reconstruction, no lifecycle or
      compaction changes
- [ ] Maintainer decision on codec/envelope/checksum
- [ ] etcd Range bridge binary transparency

## AI assistance disclosure

The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and can defend the change
end-to-end.

title: [TransferEngine] Reuse selectTransport across consecutive same-target_id requests
body:
## Description

`submitTransfer` currently calls `selectTransport` for every request. Consecutive
requests against the same `target_id` repeat the metadata lookup even when the
segment advertises a single protocol.

This change keeps the previous `Transport*` when `target_id` is unchanged and
the last lookup allowed reuse. Reuse is allowed only for a single-protocol
segment; mixed-protocol segments (comma in `protocol`) still route each request
by `target_offset`. Invalid segment IDs clear the reuse flag.

Measured `submitTransfer` p50 on same-host H20 / `mlx5_bond_0` RDMA (classic
tebench, VRAM, GPU0→GPU1 READ, 4 KiB blocks). First two iterations skipped.
Wait / bandwidth is completion time and is not claimed. Baseline is current
`origin/main` (already includes #4259).

This is the best case: tebench talks to one target, so every request after the
first reuses the lookup. A batch that rotates peers gets no submit-side win.

| batch | origin/main | this PR | change |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 4,096 | 1.654 ms | 1.524 ms | −8% |
| 65,536 | 17.642 ms | 14.636 ms | −17% |
| 207,360 | 52.644 ms | 43.072 ms | −18% |

## How Has This Been Tested?

**Test commands:**

title: [TransferEngine] Add optional tebench submit/wait JSONL log
body:
## Description

`tebench` `Avg Tx` wraps `submitTransfer` and completion wait in one timer, so the two phases cannot be split for control-path analysis.

This PR adds optional `--split_output_jsonl=<path>` (empty by default). When set on the initiator, each completed transfer appends one JSON line:

```json
{"batch_size":207360,"submit_us":66874,"wait_us":556363,"polls":201}
```

When disabled, the hot path checks a flag once: no extra timers, no file open, no `getenv`. When enabled, the file is opened once as `std::ofstream` and written with stream buffering; there is no per-line flush.

Wired for both classic and TENT. This is an analysis tool and does not change default `BW` / `Avg Tx` meaning. `wait_us` is not an application poll interval.

title: [Store] Persist and recover DFS allocator metadata
body:
## Description

Implements the standalone DFS allocator recovery proposed in #3819.

Previously, `DfsGlobalAllocator` lost allocation ownership on Master restart, allowing ranges referenced by restored metadata to be reused. This change persists allocator state in per-shard checkpoints and WALs, then reconciles recovered allocations with standalone Master snapshots before serving requests.

- Persist `ALLOC` before exposing a descriptor and `RELEASE` before reusing a deferred extent.
- Recover allocator state from checksummed checkpoints and WAL records, with configurable compaction.
- Keep the allocator sealed during snapshot reconciliation. Retain matching DFS replicas, prune stale descriptors, and quarantine orphan allocations for a fresh deferred-free interval.
- Reject incomplete, corrupt, or incompatible metadata.
- Preserve online shard expansion and recover both existing and newly added shard allocations after restart.

Two details adapt the RFC to the current implementation:
- Compatibility validation uses stable per-shard identity rather than the total shard count, so online expansion does not invalidate existing checkpoints.
- The WAL compaction setting is named `MOONCAKE_DFS_METADATA_WAL_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD_BYTES`.

### Compatibility and scope

The DFS descriptor format and client data path remain unchanged. Existing roots containing only `.data` files cannot be migrated in place; upgrade and rollback require a new empty DFS root.

This supports standalone Master recovery. HA, OpLog recovery, standby promotion, and multi-tenant DFS remain unsupported. Allocator metadata persistence does not add data-file `fsync` durability.

title: [Store] Add Intel XPU host-staging path to the Store client, Python e2e and vLLM-XPU smoke tests
body:
## Description

This is **PR3** of the Intel XPU enablement series (RFC #4031; PR1 #4030 added
the TENT XPU platform, PR2 #4157 added the XPU transport, routing and
host-staging in the Transfer Engine). It brings the Mooncake Store client up on
Intel XPU and adds end-to-end acceptance tests against an unmodified vLLM-XPU.

**Store**
- `mooncake-store/src/device/xpu_accelerator_device.cpp` (new, built only under
  `USE_XPU`): a SYCL-backed `AcceleratorDevice` (vendor `kIntel`). It
  classifies any USM pointer against the platform default context (the one
  PyTorch allocates from), so foreign device memory is recognised; copies run
  on queues bound to that context; pinned host memory comes from
  `sycl::malloc_host`. Linked in through `EnsureXpuAcceleratorDeviceLinked()`.
- `accelerator_device.h` / `accelerator_registry.cpp`: `kIntel` vendor and the
  registration hook.
- `mooncake-store/src/CMakeLists.txt`: add the source and a `USE_XPU` branch in
  the D2H-staging block.

**icpx compile fixes** (behaviour-neutral for GCC)
- vendored `fmt` 8.0.1 `core.h`: two upstream-equivalent fixes so the
  `consteval` `FMT_STRING` checks compile under clang-based compilers.
- `client_service.cpp`: define `Client::BatchUpsert` after `PutOperation` is
  complete (`std::vector<PutOperation>` was instantiated on an incomplete type).

**Engine selection is unchanged** (per review on #4157): Intel XPU is only
supported by the TENT engine, so XPU deployments must set `MC_USE_TENT=1`. The
smoke scripts default it via `os.environ.setdefault`, the Python XPU test skips
unless it is set, and the `MC_USE_TENT` row in the store deployment guide notes
the requirement.

**Tests**
- `pybind_client_test`: `XpuDeviceBufferPutGetRoundTrips` (`put_from` /
  `get_into` on `sycl::malloc_device` buffers, byte-equal), compiled with
  `MOONCAKE_TEST_XPU_H2D` under `USE_XPU`.
- `mooncake-wheel/tests/test_put_get_tensor.py`: `test_xpu_local_copy_paths`
  (`put_tensor` / `upsert_tensor` from `device="xpu"`, `get_tensor_into_cuda`
  into a registered XPU tensor, 4 MiB `put_from` / `get_into` round trip). The
  class now closes the store in `tearDownClass`: leaving it to the process-exit
  backstop tears the client down from a C `atexit` handler after the
  interpreter and the SYCL runtime have finalized, which on XPU intermittently
  aborted in `free()` while joining the client's worker threads.
- `scripts/xpu/vllm_store_smoke.py`: one vLLM instance on an Intel XPU with
  vLLM's V1 `MooncakeStoreConnector` (`kv_role=kv_both`) and local prefix
  caching disabled. Request 1 prefills and the connector saves the KV blocks
  into Mooncake Store (XPU KV cache → host staging → segment); request 2 is
  identical, cannot hit vLLM's own prefix cache, so the connector loads the
  blocks back into the XPU KV cache and decode resumes from them. PASS requires
  identical non-empty greedy tokens and connector metrics showing
  `save_put` / `load_get` keys with zero failures.
- `scripts/xpu/vllm_store_pd_smoke.py`: a vLLM `kv_producer` on one XPU
  (embedded Mooncake segment + master) and a `kv_consumer` on another
  (standalone-store, no segment), so every decode-side load is a real
  cross-device pull from the prefill segment. `--role local` spawns both on one
  node with `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:{0,1}`; `--role prefill` /
  `--role decode` run the halves on separate nodes.
- Both scripts carry two in-process shims for vLLM ≤ 0.29 code that is
  CUDA-specific rather than Mooncake-specific, to be dropped once fixed
  upstream: the connector's `wait_for_save` uses `torch.cuda.Event` (a raising
  dummy on XPU torch → aliased to `torch.xpu.Event`), and
  `ChunkedTokenDatabase.prepare_values` computes KV addresses in `np.int64`,
  which overflows on Level Zero USM pointers (≥ 2^63) → `uint64` math (the
  Mooncake bindings already take `uintptr_t`). Because of the shims the engine
  core runs in-process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`).
