title: [Transfer Engine] Optimize RDMA scatter reads
body:
## Description

Optimize generic scatter READs with an adaptive direct-vs-gather path in
Transfer Engine. Many small source ranges are packed on the data owner into
pre-registered Store buffer-pool memory, then transferred as a small number of
bulk RDMA WRITEs. Large ranges stay on the existing direct path.

Design RFC: #4242.

The implementation includes:

- A workload- and RDMA-aware planner in `TransferEngine::submitScatter`.
- Owner-side packing with packing/RDMA overlap and bounded pipeline depth.
- Pre-registered staging memory supplied by the existing Store buffer pool.
- Compact relative-offset encoding for up to 131,072 source spans per command.
- Parallel request shards for pure many-small-range workloads.
- A single gather pipeline beside direct transfers for mixed small/large loads.
- Direct-scatter fallback when capability negotiation, staging allocation,
  validation, or active gather fails.
- Batch completion for contiguous fragment runs while preserving the existing
  per-fragment callback API.

The policy is implemented once in Transfer Engine. Existing Store ranged reads
and Reshard callers that reach `submitScatter` use the same planner and fallback
without module-specific implementations. Structured Object is intentionally not
rewired in this PR; that change needs a separate before/after benchmark.

This PR does not change global QP, CQ, READ-credit, pinned-memory,
`remote_accessible`, or other RDMA defaults.

### Cost model

For payload `S`, fragment count `N`, coalesced span count `M`, detected link
bandwidth `B`, RTT `L`, effective queue depth `Q`, and candidate pipeline depth
`P`:

```text
T_direct = L + max(S/B, N/R_post, ceil(N/Q)*L)

s_limit = B_mem * (1/R_post + L/Q - 1/R_copy)

C(P) = align_64KiB(clamp(max(2*B*L/P, B*250us, S/P), 1MiB, 16MiB))
K    = ceil(S/C)

T_pack   = S/B_mem + M/R_copy
T_bulk   = L + max(S/B, K/R_post, ceil(K/Q)*L)
T_gather = T_control + min(S,C)/B_mem
           + max(T_pack,T_bulk) + min(T_pack,T_bulk)/P
           + min(S,C)/B
```

The planner evaluates `P in {1, 2, 4}` up to the available staging/CPU width
and selects gather only when `1.10 * T_gather < T_direct`. `B` and `Q` are
derived from active RDMA contexts and configured QP capacity; there are no
NIC-model, token-count, or topology-specific branches.

### Dependencies

- No unmerged Mooncake PR is required. #4095 is already in `main`; this PR does
  not duplicate its metadata snapshot reuse.
- #4083 is the latest EngramStore interface and is a downstream consumer of the
  generic path.

title: [TE] Honor the protocol hint when selecting Ascend Direct
body:
## Description

A classic (non-TENT) transfer engine built with `-DUSE_ASCEND_DIRECT=ON` installed the Ascend Direct transport on every `init()`, so the protocol hint was ignored and `protocol="rdma"` still landed on Ascend Direct.

The protocol hint now selects the transport when Ascend Direct is compiled in:

| protocol hint | installed transport |
| --- | --- |
| not set, `ascend`, `ascend_direct` | Ascend Direct |
| `rdma` (any other name) | the pre-existing host-transport selection (RDMA/TCP auto-discover, `MC_FORCE_TCP`, ...) |

The Ascend branch returns as soon as it installs, so a hint that names a host transport never also installs Ascend Direct (and vice versa). `registerLocalMemory` walks every installed transport, so keeping both in one engine is not safe.

The hint now reaches the classic engine through the `protocol` argument of `init()`, which was previously discarded. An empty argument leaves the protocol stored by `setAutoDiscover()` untouched, which is how Mooncake Store passes the client protocol before calling `init()`; `TransferEnginePy::initialize(..., protocol)` takes effect through the same path. `MC_FORCE_TCP` / `MC_FORCE_SHM` are still handled before transport selection and keep their precedence.

Transport selection is driven by the hint alone, not by `AutoDiscoverConfig::enabled`, so an NPU build keeps installing Ascend for callers that leave auto-discovery on by default (Python) and for callers that turn it off (Store). No Python binding, CMake, or docs changes are needed.

**Behavior changes to be aware of**

- A caller that passes a host protocol (for example `rdma`) to an Ascend Direct build now gets the host transport instead of Ascend Direct. That is the fix, but a caller that relied on the hint being ignored should pass `ascend` or nothing.
- With auto-discovery disabled and a host hint, `init()` installs no transport, exactly as it does in every other build; the caller installs one with `installTransport()`, which is what Store and the Python binding already do. The engine logs the hint and which branch it took.
- A hint naming a transport the build does not provide is dropped rather than forwarded, so `protocol="efa"` on a build without `USE_EFA` keeps discovering RDMA/TCP instead of failing the install. In a `USE_EFA` build the same hint now selects EFA, and the Python binding is unaffected: its EFA path builds the engine with auto-discovery off and installs EFA itself.
- HCCL builds (`USE_ASCEND` without `USE_ASCEND_DIRECT`) always install Ascend, unchanged: the transport decision is constant-true there, so the host-selection block below it is never reached.
- The host-selection block is no longer wrapped in a build-time gate, so it is compiled in every build, HCCL included. It used to be compiled out for HCCL builds; nothing about that configuration's runtime behavior changes, but it now has to keep compiling there.

## Module

- [x] Transfer Engine (`mooncake-transfer-engine`)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## How Has This Been Tested?

**Test commands:**
```bash
# Lima VM (aarch64), CANN 9.2.0, -DUSE_ASCEND_DIRECT=ON (USE_ASCEND=OFF, USE_TCP=ON, USE_TENT=OFF)
cmake -DUSE_ASCEND_DIRECT=ON ..
make transport_uint_test
./transport_uint_test --gtest_filter='TransferEngine*'
MC_FORCE_TCP=1 ./transport_uint_test
./scripts/code_format.sh --check --changed-lines --base upstream/main
```

**Test results:**
- [x] Unit tests pass
- [ ] Integration tests pass (if applicable)
- [x] Manual testing done (describe below)

- `TransferEngine*`: 8/8 pass, including 5 new cases. `InitProtocolHintReachesEngine` drives the real wiring (`TransferEngine::init(..., "rdma")` → `applyProtocolHint` → recorded protocol) and the run logs `protocol=rdma, skipping Ascend Direct for the host transports`; `RdmaHintNeverInstallsAscendDirect` (DIRECT builds only) checks over the public API that `init()` returns 0 and `getTransport("ascend")` stays null — before this change the same call returned -1 on this host, because the Ascend install it forced has no NPU to attach to.
- Full `transport_uint_test` with `MC_FORCE_TCP=1`: 32/32 pass.
- Compile check for the one configuration whose build changes: `transfer_engine_impl.cpp` compiled clean with an HCCL macro set (`-DUSE_ASCEND`, no `USE_ASCEND_DIRECT`). A full `-DUSE_ASCEND=ON` build cannot be configured in this VM — it links `MPI::MPI` under `USE_ASCEND` and the VM has no MPI — and HCCL was not exercised at runtime (no NPU). No CI workflow builds a pure HCCL configuration either (`ci_ascend.yml` and `release-npu.yaml` both pass `-DUSE_ASCEND_DIRECT=ON`), so this one is on manual verification.
- Full `transport_uint_test` on the default path: 18 pass, 14 `TransportTest.*` cases fail because the VM has no NPU. Those cases call `init()` without a protocol, so they land on the Ascend path both before and after this change (`Failed to install Ascend transport` / `cannot allocate local segment`, `init()` returning -1): an environment limitation, not a regression. The same -1 is what a `protocol="rdma"` call used to get on this host, which is what the new DIRECT case asserts away.
- Not run: RDMA/Ascend data-path tests (no HCAs or NPU in the VM). `ascend_transport` is named on the link line together with `libllm_datadist`, which CANN 9.2.0 no longer ships, so the test binary was linked with `-Wl,--allow-shlib-undefined` — the same workaround `ascend_direct_transport_test` already uses for unresolved Ascend shlib symbols.
- CI caveat: `.github/workflows/ci_ascend.yml` builds with `BUILD_UNIT_TESTS=OFF`, so the `USE_ASCEND_DIRECT` branch of the new helper is not compiled by any job. It was exercised locally as above; re-running this suite on a machine with an NPU would cover it in CI if `BUILD_UNIT_TESTS` is ever enabled there.

title: [TENT] Fall back to the control plane when the RDMA notification channel is unavailable
body:
## Description

Three failures in `RdmaTransport::sendNotification()` mean nothing left the host: no endpoint could be brought up for the peer, the endpoint has no connected notify QP, or the post was refused. All three surfaced as `InternalError`, which the engine handed back as the final answer, so the notification was simply gone. Two gaps sat behind it: `receiveNotification()` drained only the first transport that supports notifications, so anything the TCP transport had queued from the control plane was never handed out; and no notify callback was registered with `ControlService` unless a TCP transport was loaded, so an RDMA-only engine dropped every RPC-delivered notification.

Measured with a two-process probe: disabling the initiator's notify QP after 500 sends left the target with 500 of 4000 notifications and no END marker, and an initiator loaded without an RDMA transport delivered 0 of 2000 to a target that had one.

Change:

- The three "nothing was posted" cases become `DeviceNotFound` / `RdmaError` instead of `InternalError`. `getEndpoint()` takes an optional `Status* failure` so the reason for a missing endpoint is not lost; the default argument keeps its signature source-compatible.
- `TransferEngineImpl::sendNotification()` tries every loaded notification transport in slot order, skips the ones whose channel is unavailable, and when all are, sends over the control-plane `Notify` RPC the peer already answers bootstrap on - the same wire path `TcpTransport::sendNotification()` uses, and what the classic engine's `rdma_notify_oob_fallback` does. Any other error is returned untouched. A transport that advertises notifications but returns `NotImplemented` is skipped on both the send chain and the receive drain. Each fallback is logged with `LOG_EVERY_N` and a running count.
- One case is deliberately excluded: when the bootstrap failed because the RPC itself failed, the peer's control plane is not answering, so the status is reported as `RpcServiceError` and the engine returns it as is rather than stacking a second RPC timeout on the polling thread. Every other reason still falls back.
- `receiveNotification()` drains every notification transport plus the in-process queue, each into its own vector because `TcpTransport::receiveNotification()` clears its argument. One transport that cannot be read does not stop the drain.
- `construct()` registers an in-process notify callback with `ControlService` before the transports install, so RPC-delivered notifications are queued even without a TCP transport; `deconstruct()` clears it.
- `notification/rpc_fallback` (default true) turns the whole thing off.

Worth knowing: the fallback is a synchronous RPC at call sites that already do one, roughly 67 us on a live peer over loopback; a payload larger than the 64 KB slot now reaches the peer over RPC instead of failing; ordering holds within one path, so notifications that came over RPC are handed out after the ones the notify QP carried in the same poll; and delivery over the fallback needs the receiver to run this change or to have a TCP transport, otherwise the result is what it is today, only no longer reported as an error. Only failures where nothing was posted are covered - a notification lost after a successful post needs receiver-side deduplication first, which comes later in the series. No wire-format and no default timeout change.

This is the third of seven PRs on notification fault tolerance, described in the series RFC (#4061). It applies to `main` on its own, using the in-process notification queue that #3464 added there.

## Module

## How Has This Been Tested?

`tent_notification_fallback_test` is new: 10 cases covering the fallback chain (both unavailable statuses), the statuses that must not fall back, the unreachable control plane returned as is, the last transport's error winning over the RPC leg, every transport being unavailable and the RPC leg taking it, the `NotImplemented` skip, the config switch, the merged receive drain, a drain that continues past a failing transport, and an RPC notification landing between two engines that have no TCP transport. Stand-in transports are swapped in through the existing `swapTransportForTest()` hook, so no NIC or metadata server is needed. `RdmaNotifyFaultTriageTest` gains two cases for the bootstrap-failure exclusion.

Negative controls, each reverted afterwards: removing the fallback loop reddens 5 of the new cases; draining only the first transport, 3; dropping the in-process callback and not skipping `NotImplemented`, one each; removing the `RpcServiceError` branch reddens the exclusion case.

| Injection | before | after |

| none | 4000/4000, 0 duplicates; transfer-bound p50/p99 168.9-170.4 / 246.9-249.0 us | 4000/4000, 0 duplicates; 170.4 / 247.3 us |
| initiator's notify QP disabled after 500 sends | 500 of 4000, 2000 send errors, END never arrived | 4000/4000, 0 duplicates, 0 send errors; standalone p50/p99 67.2 / 120.0 us over RPC |
| initiator loaded without an RDMA transport | 0 of 2000 (queued by the target, never drained) | 2000/2000, 0 duplicates; p50/p99 66.6 / 119.5 us |
| peer frozen before any endpoint exists, two `sendNotification()` calls | 30.009 s, 30.001 s | 30.009 s, 30.001 s, no fallback attempted; without the exclusion above, 90.011 s and 60.001 s |

title: [TENT] Retry read-only segment metadata lookup once after RPC failure
body:
## Description

Retry `ControlClient::getSegmentDesc` once when the first attempt returns an
RPC service error. The failed stale connection is discarded by the existing
RPC agent, so the bounded retry can establish a fresh connection after a peer
restarts on the same address.

The retry is intentionally limited to this read-only metadata lookup. Other
control-plane RPCs may have side effects and retain their existing
single-attempt behavior. The healthy path still performs one RPC, while a
persistent failure performs at most two attempts and returns the second error.

This change adds loopback RPC coverage for same-port restart recovery,
thread-local stale connection pools, persistent failures, healthy-path call
count, and the non-replay contract for mutating notifications. It does not
change any public API, wire format, or configuration.

This is the first staged implementation change described by RFC #4162 and
prepares the metadata recovery path for the later congestion-control work.

Related RFC: [#4162](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/4162)

title: [Reshard] Add Store-backed model-weight snapshots
body:
## Description

This PR adds Store-backed model-weight snapshots for heterogeneous resharding.

`WeightStore` persists a complete, immutable `StoredWeightManifest` only after
all planned payload fragments have been uploaded and verified. The manifest is
address-free and retains the logical tensor/fragment layout required to plan a
later restore into a different target topology. Runtime GPU addresses,
allocation bounds, leases, and allocation guards stay in ephemeral runtime
bindings.

The Store path provides:

- generation-consistent source replica selection and upload planning;
- grouped payload and metadata records through Mooncake Store;
- commit/abort decisions, payload completeness checks, and recovery-safe
  registration cleanup;
- retry-safe manifest publication after a commit decision;
- range-based restore with `get_into_ranges` into validated target bindings;
- an explicit `WeightStoreWriter` lifecycle:
  `begin_weight_snapshot(...) -> write_tensor(...) -> commit()`.

### Breaking Change and Migration

This PR removes the public `*_with_parallelism` API family and the associated
`ParallelAxis`, `TensorParallelism`, and `ReadTarget` helper types.

Model-weight snapshot writers migrate to:

```python
writer = WeightStore(store).begin_weight_snapshot(descriptor, adapter)
writer.write_tensor(tensor_id, tensor)
manifest = writer.commit()
```

The writer stores manifest-managed payload fragments and publishes one
`StoredWeightManifest`; it does not create ordinary Store tensor objects.
After a manifest publication failure that follows the Store commit decision,
the writer preserves its payloads and remains available for `commit()` retry.
Snapshot readers migrate to `load_manifest()`, `plan_load()`, and `load()`
with target placement and runtime binding manifests. The existing single-axis
TP `*_with_tp` APIs remain separate compatibility APIs.

The native Store adapter requires `ReplicateConfig.group_ids`, supplied by the
merged Store group-semantics support. Transfer Engine lowering and live G2G
execution remain in the follow-up PR.

title: [Reshard] Bind logical transfer plans to runtime snapshots
body:
## Description

This PR adds the late runtime-binding and physical-attestation layer for
heterogeneous model-weight resharding.

The preceding logical-planning layer produces an address-free
`LogicalTransferPlan`: it identifies the required source and target logical
regions, but deliberately has no GPU address, allocation, endpoint, lease, or
runtime-instance information. This PR consumes that plan together with typed
`WeightRuntimeBindingManifest` inputs and returns an attested `TransferPlan`.
The resulting plan contains selected runtime fragments and executor
projections for a later backend to consume.

Binding is fail-closed. It verifies source and target placement identity and
digest, revision and weight generation, participant selection, runtime
fragment geometry, device/address/allocation bounds, lease metadata, target
coverage, alias scope, and executor snapshots. It also rejects forged or
reconstructed plans whose physical evidence no longer matches the planned
placement.

The returned `TransferPlan` is a validated runtime snapshot, not an execution
API.

title: [Reshard] Add N-D logical weight transfer planner
body:
## Description

This PR adds the address-free logical-planning phase for heterogeneous
model-weight resharding in the new `mooncake-reshard` module.

It consumes complete typed source and target placements, or a committed logical
`WeightManifest` Store snapshot as the source, and produces a backend-neutral
`LogicalTransferPlan`. The plan contains compact N-D `TransferRegion` values:
logical overlap offsets and shapes, source/target base byte offsets,
`inner_bytes`, outer loop counts, and source/target strides.

The planner supports different source and target TP / PP / EP / DP layouts
without embedding framework-specific tensor-name parsing or model-layout
inference in Mooncake core:

- TP and EP use N-D logical-box split and merge, including different source
  and target shard dimensions.
- PP routes through explicit, framework-provided tensor or layer ownership;
  it does not infer stages from parameter names or layer-count formulas.
- EP is represented by a logical expert coordinate, so independent expert
  allocations remain independent fragments rather than being packed or
  all-gathered.
- DP selects a complete source replica or follows explicit DP ownership
  without changing tensor geometry.

The planner validates canonical resource identity, revision, weight
generation, tensor descriptors, ownership, logical coverage, aliases, and
planning limits. It keeps N-D regions compact and fails closed when a later
segment expansion would exceed its explicit limit.

This PR intentionally does not add runtime GPU binding, address or allocation
validation, lease attestation, Mooncake Store persistence/lifecycle, Transfer
Engine lowering/execution, model-specific packing or quantization conversion,
or framework runtime-object parsing. Those belong to later phases.

title: [Reshard] Add resource and model-weight manifest contracts
body:
## Description

Related RFC: #3111

This PR introduces the manifest contract layer for `mooncake-reshard`. It defines framework-neutral resource identity and the first model-weight specialization without coupling Mooncake Core to SGLang, vLLM, PyTorch, model-specific parameter names, Mooncake Store, or a transfer backend.

The central contract is that one `WeightPlacementManifest` describes one complete, address-free global logical placement of a model-weight generation. Framework-owned adapters on each worker export local `WeightPlacementPart` values; a collection barrier assembles and validates the exact part set before a stable placement ID and digest are produced. Live GPU addresses remain in per-participant `WeightRuntimeBindingManifest` values and are validated immediately before use.

Later PRs add the backend-neutral N-D planner, Store integration, and Transfer Engine lowering under the same `mooncake-reshard` namespace.

### What This PR Adds

#### 1. Resource-neutral contracts

- `ResourceManifest`: resource identity and kind;
- `PlacementManifest`: stable, address-free placement identity and digest;
- `RuntimeBindingManifest`: ephemeral physical state fenced by placement identity, runtime instance, generation, and lease;
- `ResourceKind.MODEL_WEIGHT`, with `KV_CACHE` reserved for a future specialization;
- shared typed placement-to-binding identity validation.

Model revision, tensor geometry, layout, parallel ownership, and weight generation remain weight-specific.

#### 2. Complete model-weight placement

`WeightPlacementManifest` contains:

- `ParallelTopology` with TP, PP, EP, and DP sizes plus an explicit participant-to-rank mapping;
- one `WeightPlacementPart` for every selected participant;
- canonical tensor descriptors and N-D logical fragments;
- model revision, weight generation, and placement-set identity;
- a placement ID and digest derived only after global validation succeeds.

`ParallelTopology.world_size` is the selected participant count, not the product of TP/PP/EP/DP sizes. Parallel axes may share workers, and a placement may select one complete DP replica while preserving the runtime's declared `dp_size`.

Global validation rejects missing or duplicate participants, mixed topology or generation identity, rank mismatches, conflicting tensor descriptors, overlapping logical boxes, and incomplete tensor coverage. PP owners are validated independently, so fragments from different PP owners cannot be combined to manufacture coverage.

#### 3. Per-participant runtime binding

Each live participant exports one `WeightRuntimeBindingManifest` that:

- identifies its `participant_id`;
- attests the complete global placement ID and digest;
- binds exactly that participant's logical fragments to worker, endpoint, device, address, and allocation owner;
- carries runtime instance, generation, and lease fences.

Empty participants require no physical binding. Any participant referenced by a later execution plan must provide a valid binding. GPU addresses and owner objects never enter the serializable placement.

#### 4. Framework-neutral tensor semantics

The weight contract records:

- stable tensor identity, global shape, dtype, and item size;
- layout fingerprint plus optional layer and expert identity;
- N-D logical boxes using `global_offset` and `local_shape`;
- TP, PP, EP, and DP owner coordinates;
- canonical `shard_dims` with explicit split, replication, and ownership axis types;
- contiguous runtime views with address-range and alias validation.

Mooncake does not infer layer, expert, partition, or layout semantics from parameter names. Framework-owned adapters must normalize those facts into the canonical typed contracts before entering Mooncake Core; framework objects are never inspected by the core.

#### 5. Packaging and documentation

The tracked source lives under `mooncake-reshard/python/mooncake/reshard`. The combined Mooncake wheel stages this package during the build and removes the staging copy on exit. The design document describes global placement assembly, identity, binding, and lifecycle boundaries.

### Why Split Placement, Parts, and Binding?

- `WeightPlacementPart` is the framework-local contribution produced independently by each selected worker.
- `WeightPlacementManifest` is the complete global logical fact used by planning and control-plane identity.
- `WeightRuntimeBindingManifest` is per-participant live physical state.

This lets logical planning start from complete source and target placements without waiting for every target GPU address. Physical binding remains late, generation-fenced, and lease-fenced.

### Non-Goals

This PR does not:

- generate heterogeneous reshard regions;
- execute Transfer Engine operations;
- persist weights in Mooncake Store;
- implement a KVCache manifest or KV resharding;
- infer model semantics from tensor names;
- define discovery, activation, rollback, or control-plane policy;
- integrate M2N, scatter batching, or another optimized executor.

Planner, Store, TE, framework-adapter, and KV-specialization work follow as separate changes.

title: [Bugfix][TransferEngine] Reconnect Redis context after I/O error (#4003)
body:
## Description

Fixes #4003.

`RedisStoragePlugin` holds a single long-lived `redisContext` and never rebuilds it. hiredis latches any I/O error into the context (`ctx->err != 0`) and then rejects every subsequent command — so a single disconnect (e.g. a load-balancer idle timeout) **permanently disables** metadata publishing and lookup for the rest of the process lifetime:

```
get()/set()/remove() return false forever
redisCommand() returns nullptr on every call
```

## Root Cause

`RedisStoragePlugin` never stored `host` / `port` and had no reconnect path. After any `REDIS_ERR_IO`, the stale context was reused indefinitely.

## Fix

- Store `host_`, `port_`, `username_`, `password_`, `db_index_` at construction time.
- Add `reconnect()`: `redisFree` → `redisConnect` → optional `AUTH` → optional `SELECT`. Returns `false` on failure (never crashes).
- Add `ensureConnected()`: checks `ctx->err` before each operation; calls `reconnect()` if non-zero.
- `get()`, `set()`, `remove()`: call `ensureConnected()` first; on `nullptr` reply, do one `reconnect()` + retry (handles mid-flight drops).

## Testing

- `RedisStoragePluginTest/BasicRoundTrip`: SET/GET/DEL round-trip; skipped via `GTEST_SKIP()` when `MC_REDIS_TEST_SERVER` is unreachable.
- `RedisStoragePluginTest/PluginWorksAfterInitialConnectionError`: verifies graceful `false` (no crash) when server is unreachable from start.

title: [Bugfix][TENT] Add non-blocking try_push to BoundedMPSCQueue and fail slices on queue full (#3636)
body:
Fixes #3636 and #3637.

## Summary

A full bounded worker queue could make BoundedMPSCQueue::push() spin forever. A worker retrying into the same queue it must drain could therefore wedge all RDMA progress.

Initial multi-worker submission also needs atomic admission. If an earlier worker observes and posts its list before a later queue rejects, asynchronous cancellation can overlap fallback and freeSubBatch(), allowing late CQ completions to reference freed slices.

## Fix

- Keep non-blocking try_push() for retry paths and return backpressure instead of spinning.
- Keep a large worker queue capacity to avoid rejection during normal bursts.
- Add queue try_reserve(), commit(), and cancel_reservation() operations.
- Add Workers::admitBatch():
  - reserve one cell in every target worker queue before publishing any real list;
  - if any reservation fails, publish only default empty placeholders for earlier reservations and return TooManyRequests;
  - after every reservation succeeds, establish ownership and inflight accounting for all lists, then commit the real lists and wake workers.
- Route RdmaTransport::submitTransferTasks() through admitBatch() rather than per-worker submit followed by asynchronous cancellation.
- Restore current upstream worker completion/retry lifecycle and remove accidentally committed conflict markers and duplicate queue methods.

No real slice list is visible to a worker on the rejection path, so no WR can be posted and no cancellation/CQ drain is required before fallback frees the sub-batch.

## Testing

- clang-format-20 --dry-run --Werror passes on all five changed C++ files.
- git diff --check passes and no merge-conflict markers remain.
- A standalone reservation regression passes:
  - reserved entries remain invisible until commit;
  - a later-queue rejection cancels earlier reservations by publishing only empty entries;
  - no real batch entry becomes visible on rejection.
- On a B200 GPU pod, USE_TENT=ON, USE_CUDA=OFF production build completes 245/245 targets, including the changed workers.cpp and rdma_transport.cpp.
- GitHub check-paths is green; remaining CTest/build/wheel/TENT jobs for head e9c337f are pending runner capacity.

title: [Perf][Integration] Reserve Python batch transfer request capacity
body:
## Description

The classic Python transfer wrapper knows the final request count before it builds synchronous, asynchronous, and CUDA-callback batches. Reserve that exact capacity before the existing `push_back` loops.

This avoids geometric `std::vector` growth and relocation while preserving request count and order, addresses, lengths, opcodes, retry fields, transport hints, submission, completion, error handling, and object lifetime.

A local component benchmark using the actual 56-byte `TransferRequest` type measured these construction-only improvements across two alternating runs:

- 1,024 descriptors: 1.17-1.19x, saving 1.55-1.83 us per vector
- 4,096 descriptors: 4.33-4.37x, saving 124-126 us per vector
- 16,384 descriptors: 5.26-5.43x, saving 664-695 us per vector

title: [TENT] Add Intel XPU transport, routing and staging to the Transfer Engine
body:
## Description

This is **PR2** of the Intel XPU enablement series for the TENT Transfer Engine
(RFC kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4031), stacked on top of the merged
**PR1** kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4030 ("Add Intel XPU platform").

It wires the Intel XPU device memory type (`MTYPE_XPU`) through the transport,
routing, and staging layers so that transfers touching XPU VRAM are staged
through host DRAM, mirroring the existing TPU precedent and the CUDA/NVLink
platform-binding model.

Scope is intentionally staging-only for this PR:
- `XpuTransport` advertises `gpu_to_dram` / `dram_to_gpu` and performs the
  device↔host copy through the concrete `XpuPlatform` (bound via `dynamic_cast`
  in `install()`, mirroring `NVLinkTransport`'s `CudaPlatform*` binding).
- `gpu_to_gpu` stays `false`; cross-node device traffic is always staged through
  host DRAM by `ProxyManager` (`findStagingPolicy`).
- GPUDirect dma-buf (PR4) and PCIe P2P `gpu_to_gpu` (PR5) are out of scope here.

Key changes:
- New `TransportType::XPU` (wire value 14) with name/parse round-trip and a
  `static_assert` pinning it to the C API `TRANSPORT_XPU`.
- `XpuTransport` (`install`/`startTransfer`/`addMemoryBuffer`), registered via
  `USE_XPU` and gated on the `transports/xpu/enable` config key. It only serves
  `LOCAL_SEGMENT_ID` (the local stage of a staged transfer).
- `XPU` is included in the default transport list, so
  `registerLocalMemory()` on XPU VRAM without an explicit transport list works.
- Routing (`getTransportType`, both legacy and `TransportSelector` paths): when
  either side of a non-local request is `MTYPE_XPU`, the staging policy is
  resolved up front and the host transport (RDMA / TCP / HP-TCP) is selected
  against the post-staging `dram_to_dram` pattern. This makes staging
  reachable even when no installed transport can touch device memory directly
  (e.g. HP-TCP-only deployments). `XPU` itself is gated on
  `local_segment` rather than `same_machine`, so same-host peer segments are
  staged instead of being routed to the local-only executor.
- The resolved staging plan (`SelectionResult::staging_params`) is carried
  through `prepareSubmit`, queued dispatch and `resubmitTransferTask`. The
  host<->host hop inside `ProxyManager` is routed as before, from the
  transports the real stage buffers carry on both sides; no hint is pinned.
  An unstaged host buffer on either side is used as-is by the cross stage, so
  it must itself carry the selected network transport (XPU-only host
  registrations do not route).
- `findStagingPolicy` adds an XPU case mirroring TPU: every device side is
  staged (including a mixed CUDA/ROCm/TPU peer, whose direct-DMA capability is
  unknown here), host DRAM sides are not, and a device side with no host DRAM
  stage location in its topology fails closed with a warning.
- Consolidated the device-memory-type predicate into a single
  `isGpuMemoryType()` in `platform.h`; both the selector routing predicate and
  the staging capability checks delegate to it, so the two paths can never
  disagree.

- `XpuSyclBackend` classifies externally allocated USM (e.g. PyTorch `torch.xpu`
  tensors never registered through the platform) via `sycl::get_pointer_type`
  on the device's default context, so foreign device pointers are reported as
  `MTYPE_XPU` and copied correctly instead of being treated as host memory.

Engine selection is untouched: XPU deployments opt in to TENT with
`MC_USE_TENT=1` exactly like every other build (an earlier revision made TENT
the default under `USE_XPU`; dropped per review).

Non-XPU routing is unchanged: the new `SelectionContext` fields
(`local_segment`, `host_staging`) default to `false` and `staging_params`
stays empty for every existing memory type. `ProxyManager` is untouched.
`SelectionContext`/`SelectionResult` gained fields, so dependents must be
rebuilt together (source-compatible, not ABI-compatible).

## Module

- [x] Transfer Engine (`mooncake-transfer-engine`)

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## How Has This Been Tested?

Built with the Intel oneAPI `icpx` compiler (2026.1.1) and run on real Intel
Arc Pro B60 hardware (`ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu`). A separate
GCC `-DUSE_XPU=OFF` build verifies the shared runtime is unaffected.

```bash

```

title: [TransferEngine]Add grouped scatter tasks for TCP
body:
## Description

TCP scatter currently creates one completion-tracking task per request, although `MultiTransport` already supports grouping adjacent requests from the same scatter operation. Large fragmented transfers therefore incur repeated per-task status checks.

Enable TCP's grouped-scatter capability, prepare every request in each grouped task, and accumulate the task's total byte count. Keep the existing TCP transfer sequence and wire protocol. Add tests for fragmented reads and writes, exactly-once callbacks, and preservation of individual fragment results when a peer rejects part of a group.

This is a focused TCP follow-up to [#3310](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/3310), which introduced grouped RDMA tasks while retaining TCP-local sequencing. The change reuses `MultiTransport`'s existing grouping and completion machinery. Store `get_into_ranges` can benefit when it uses TCP scatter; no Store or KV reshard changes are required by this PR.

### Performance

Configuration:

- One Linux host; two Transfer Engine instances in the same process, using real loopback TCP and CPU buffers.
- Release builds with identical options; TCP connection pooling enabled. Store, CUDA, TENT and event-driven completion disabled.
- READ transfers with 128-byte fragments, contiguous source ranges and gaps between destination ranges.
- Public `submitScatter()` plus `wait()` timed together; no Store/SGLang path.
- A–B–B–A execution order; one warm-up then seven samples per configuration per run. Values below are medians of 14 samples per version.
- Caller CPU uses `CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID`; process CPU uses `CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID` and includes both endpoints' I/O threads. CPU time sums thread execution and may exceed wall time.

All times are milliseconds per operation. Each cell shows baseline → patched.

| Fragments / payload | Actual scatter tasks | Caller-thread CPU | Process CPU | Wall time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 128 B | 1 → 1 | 0.010 → 0.010 | 0.037 → 0.036 | 0.072 → 0.072 |
| 4,096 / 512 KiB | 4,096 → 1 | 77.840 → 2.995 | 178.668 → 105.162 | 77.903 → 78.800 |
| 32,768 / 4 MiB | 32,768 → 1 | 623.128 → 18.926 | 1,426.123 → 822.338 | 623.195 → 618.878 |

For the 4 MiB case, caller-thread CPU fell by 96.96% and process CPU by 42.34%. This is a CPU-overhead reduction, not a claim of a material transfer-latency or throughput improvement.

title: [TENT] Reduce HP TCP READ receive overhead
body:
## Description

HP TCP READ uses 1 MiB chunks, but Asio's default `transfer_all` caps each underlying receive request at 64 KiB. Pass the remaining chunk length as the completion condition so the socket can receive more already-available data per operation. The existing chunk boundary, error checks, timeout and cancellation handling remain intact.

Three production lines; no new state, configuration, locks or scheduling. Add socket coverage for fragmented payloads, truncated tails and stalled tails.

Paired qjh007/qjh006 host-memory measurements, two rails, CPU and memory on NUMA 0, three interleaved repetitions per version, unchanged server:

| Workload | Baseline | Change | Gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| tebench 64 MiB READ, 16 workers/connections/callers | 25.31 GB/s | 27.17 GB/s | 7.3% |
| Store 8 MiB READ, 4 workers/connections, 4 callers | 7.33 GB/s | 8.05 GB/s | 9.8% |

Median client CPU: 27.59→27.65 cores for tebench, 6.80→6.60 for Store. Server CPU: 6.60→6.94 and 1.75→1.95 respectively. Client CPU per GB falls 6.6% / 11.6%; Store p99 is effectively unchanged (9.22→9.27 ms). These are host-memory READ results, not GPU or full-model measurements. title: [TE] Bound pooled TCP admission by queued bytes
body:
## Description

Classic TCP currently bounds each connection group's waiting work by item
count. Because each item retains its source payload until it starts or leaves
the waiting queues, large requests can retain a much larger byte extent than
the item limits suggest. This became more important after #3710 raised the
default queue and pending-admission limits to 65,535. Its review identified a
byte-based limit as follow-up work.

This change adds the opt-in `MC_TCP_MAX_QUEUED_BYTES_PER_PEER` setting. For each
TCP `ConnectionKey`, it bounds:

```text
sum(queue.length) + sum(pending_admissions.length)
```

A request that would exceed the limit receives the existing `QUEUE_FULL`
terminal result. Moving an item from pending admission to the queue is
accounting-neutral; its charge is released when it starts on a lane or leaves a
waiting container through timeout, error, retirement, or shutdown.

Unset or `0` preserves existing behavior. Active lanes are excluded because
their count is already bounded by `MC_TCP_LANES_PER_PEER`. The limit remains
opt-in because selecting a nonzero default requires representative
slow/stalled-peer and caller-recovery measurements.

Admission is per transport work item, not atomic over a multi-descriptor
`batchTransferSync` call. An earlier descriptor can be accepted before a later
one is rejected. The documentation therefore warns callers not to treat a
nonzero batch result as proof that no destination bytes changed or that all
source buffers can immediately be released.

This is a resource-admission bound, not a throughput or RSS-reduction claim.

Related: #2930, #3710, #3446

title: [Bugfix] Reconnect idle TCP lanes after peer close
body:
## Description

Before reusing an idle TCP lane, peek at its socket to detect a peer that has closed the connection. On EOF or socket error, discard the stale socket and allow the lane to reconnect on the next pump round. title: Mooncake EPD: Multimodal and Agent-State Disaggregation
body:
# Mooncake EPD: Multimodal and Agent-State Disaggregation

## Summary

This integration PR adds Encoder-Prefill-Decode disaggregation to Mooncake and
vLLM. It adds real Vision Hidden State transfer, layered paged-KV handoff,
multimodal hidden-state reuse, Agent KV state cloning, state-aware scheduling,
backpressure, and artifact-gated evaluation.

The implementation is organized along existing Mooncake ownership boundaries
so Transfer Engine, Store, vLLM integration, serving control plane, tests, and
benchmarks can be reviewed independently.

## Follow-up development since PR #2836 was opened

The comparison baseline for this section is the original PR head
`6f6514cc8bb8ff468c0da31ec9e587058177e849`. It covers all subsequent local
development, not only the latest prompt/Decode/scheduler optimization.

**Diff boundary:** `6f6514cc` is retained as the original-review baseline.
The follow-up implementation below is included by the subsequent PR branch
update, so reviewers can distinguish the initially submitted code from the
new reliability, state-management, and performance-remediation changes.

### 1. Mooncake integration and vLLM compatibility boundary

- Moved the standalone prototype into the Mooncake source tree as an optional
  `mooncake_epd` package with explicit runtime, test, benchmark, and vLLM
  integration boundaries.
- Added a pinned vLLM compatibility contract, startup probes, capability
  reporting, generated worker configuration, and an explicit adapter surface
  under `integrations/vllm/`.
- Scoped workspace patches behind `MOONCAKE_EPD_ENABLE_VLLM_PATCHES=1`;
  ordinary Mooncake and non-EPD vLLM startup keep their existing behavior.
- Added CPU and self-hosted hardware CI tiers. Missing GPU, RDMA, model, or
  second-host capability is recorded as a skip/unavailable result, never as a
  successful transport claim.

### 2. Encoder-to-Prefill Feature State

- Replaced ad-hoc hidden-state payloads with versioned
  `FeatureStateManifestV2` descriptors that bind model/processor identity,
  tensor shape/dtype/layout, checksums, source generation, destination,
  lifetime, and multimodal structure.
- Added Prefill-owned direct feature buffers with authenticated allocation,
  readiness, generation fences, reference counting, leases, bounded cache,
  transaction cleanup, and explicit release.
- Added `epd-direct://` resolution in vLLM and injection of precomputed
  `image_embeds`, DeepStack intermediates, and `grid_thw`, allowing Prefill to
  skip duplicate Vision Encoder execution.
- Coalesced same-session multi-image FeatureBundles into one Mooncake
  peer-buffer publish and one batched direct read into final hidden-state
  tensors. Different sessions remain isolated and source tensor ownership is
  retained until completion.
- Added cache prefetch, singleflight/coalescing, mutation isolation, and
  instrumentation for cold, warm, and mixed hidden-state reuse.

### 3. Prefill-to-Decode KV handoff and transport integrity

- Added `KVTransferManifestV2`, binding workflow/handoff IDs, source and
  destination generations, model/KV-layout checksums, block groups, transport,
  lease, expiry, and target worker identity.
- Enforced validation at both Decode and the Prefill producer immediately
  before export, preventing stale-generation, wrong-target, expired, tampered,
  or layout-incompatible transfers.
- Connected grouped/layered descriptors to the vLLM KV connector save/load
  lifecycle with prepare, commit, rollback, release, progress, cancellation,
  and restart cleanup.
- Added registered-pointer and peer-buffer batch transfer paths, bounded
  descriptor/byte groups, topology evidence, bandwidth/registration/lock-wait
  telemetry, and strict fallback/failure counters.
- Hardened Mooncake TCP and intra-node NVLink paths: registration ownership,
  CUDA stream/event ordering, partial transfer handling, and receive-side
  lifetime are no longer inferred from a successful API return alone.

### 4. Request-path and TTFT optimization

- Added a generation-fenced, bounded cache for deterministic strict
  `render_generate` results. Dynamic workflow IDs, FeatureHandles, and fresh KV
  handoff metadata are excluded from the cache value/key as appropriate;
  mutable external media bypasses reuse.
- Added strict prompt-only Prefill capability negotiation. The worker contract
  binds vLLM/model/tokenizer/chat-template/KV-schema identities and returns the
  exact prompt token IDs, multimodal placeholders, renderer hashes, and
  bounded structural metadata required by Decode.
- Added a versioned, fail-closed Decode token envelope. Decode consumes exact
  token IDs plus KV handoff metadata without receiving original
  image/video/audio bytes or reapplying the chat template.
- Reconstructs only integrity-bound structural inputs such as
  `image_grid_thw` locally on Decode. Prompt, placeholder, renderer, sampling,
  worker-generation, or manifest mismatches are rejected; measured strict mode
  does not silently fall back to legacy media dispatch.
- Added stage timing for request read/parse, JSON encode, Prefill render and
  generate, Decode dispatch/stream-open/first-content, connector transfer,
  lock wait, payload bytes, and per-stage queueing.

### 5. Agent State Cloning and Store-backed lifecycle

- Defined precise clone semantics: same-node physical zero-copy means retained
  immutable page references; cross-node fork is a metadata-only manifest clone
  followed by explicit materialization before a branch writes.
- Added versioned KV state manifests, Mooncake Store page objects, content
  checksums, reference accounting, Copy-on-Write, fencing tokens, and
  last-reference garbage collection.
- Added a persistent `AgentStateCatalog` with WAL recovery, CAS transitions,
  leases, state/page ownership, branch lineage, idempotent release, and orphan
  cleanup.
- Added `VLLMKVMaterializer` and a strict connector-commit boundary. Importing
  Store pages is not reported as Decode-consumable until the version-compatible
  vLLM connector callback acknowledges the target block envelope.
- Added register/fork/materialize/release control-plane APIs and lifecycle
  tests for duplicate operations, crash recovery, stale leases, and cleanup.

### 6. Agent PD scheduling and backpressure

- Added round-robin, least-loaded, static task-type, and agent-aware policies
  for thinking, interactive, and hybrid workloads.
- Split worker/request lifecycle into
  `queued → running → first_token → completed/failed/cancelled`, with
  idempotent failure, cancellation, timeout, and restart release.
- Added queued/running/active token gauges, Prefill service EWMA, Decode
  first-token/TPOT/output-rate telemetry, GPU/KV capacity, HTTP queue, transfer
  backlog/bandwidth, and native-engine lock wait.
- Telemetry now has freshness, TTL, known/unknown state, and confidence.
  Missing data is neutral/uncertain rather than incorrectly treated as zero
  load.
- Replaced the fixed affinity bonus with an explainable
  queue/service/transfer/control time-cost model, bounded topology benefit,
  congestion escape, re-entry hysteresis, and affinity/rebind statistics.

### 7. Hidden State Prefix Cache

- Added stable exact-cache keys covering input content, model and processor
  revisions, multimodal grids, dtype/layout, schema, and mutation boundaries.
- Added native L1 event synchronization, Store-backed L2 manifests,
  checksum/lease validation, prefetch, singleflight, and recovery.
- Kept partial multimodal prefix reuse experimental and disabled by default.
  It can only activate after a model-specific semantic oracle proves the
  reused `[A, B] → [A, C]` state is correct.

### 8. Omni worker-level pipeline

- Added independent-process AR → Generation → Diffusion stage envelopes with
  cancellation, timeout, lifecycle, and per-edge transport evidence.
- Implemented POSIX-SHM descriptor transfer and a real loopback TCP relay for
  CPU tensors; large tensor payloads are not mislabeled Python pickle copies.
- CUDA IPC/NVLink and RDMA remain capability-gated. Requesting unavailable
  RDMA returns `skipped`/`claim_supported=false` rather than relabeling
  TCP/SHM/CUDA copies as RDMA.
- Added Qwen2.5-Omni worker adapters and benchmark entrypoints while retaining
  an explicit boundary between synthetic transport validation and full
  model-semantic GPU validation.

### 9. Benchmark, dataset, and evidence framework

- Added reproducible Qwen-VL dataset generation with content hashes,
  workload manifests, model preflight, fixed sampling, cold/warm/mixed cache
  profiles, text controls, and W0-W5 request shapes.
- Added colocated vLLM, 1P1D/2P2D EPD, Agent clone, Hidden Cache, Omni, and
  scheduler runners with warmup/measured separation and resource topology.
- Added artifact schemas and fail-closed gates for exact/reference output,
  real service identity, prompt/KV generations, transport backend, checksums,
  fallback, cleanup, resource fairness, and performance-claim scope.
- Added request throughput, output-token throughput, TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT,
  latency, goodput, bytes, bandwidth, cache reuse, queueing, GPU/KV load,
  affinity, failures, and orphan-state metrics.
- Added `README.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `EVALUATION.md`, benchmark protocol,
  upstream vLLM split plan, CI workflows, and a compact public evidence
  snapshot with source digests.

### 10. Real-system findings and measured optimizations

- The public Qwen3-VL real EPD artifact validates Vision hidden-state reuse,
  layered KV transfer, strict no-fallback execution, and scale-out capacity.
  The recorded 4-GPU 2P2D versus 1-GPU colocated comparison is explicitly a
  capacity result, not an equal-resource efficiency claim.
- A strict single-host TCP refresh completed 4/4 measured requests with mean
  TTFT 255.93 ms, zero fallback/layered failures, and zero live direct-buffer
  references after release.
- The strict rendered-Prefill-cache ablation preserved exact outputs. At C1 it
  improved TTFT 276.90→210.19 ms (-24.1%) and completion throughput
  25.18→28.80 tok/s (+14.4%); at C4 it improved TTFT
  469.05→379.13 ms (-19.2%) and completion throughput
  71.77→78.97 tok/s (+10.0%).
- A real Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct 1E1P1D W3/C1 token-envelope smoke on GPUs 5/1/3
  exactly matched shadow mode and all six measured colocated baseline outputs
  (SHA-256
  `c29089b34feccc282a94d04d4e6f1f6f350031cc8ecd79e436ea0d7a35f92c4c`).
  Active token dispatch reduced the Decode request 1,145,006→16,718 bytes
  (-98.54%), JSON encode 18.361→0.766 ms (-95.83%), Decode stream-open
  61.347→8.239 ms (-86.57%), TTFT 378.245→341.123 ms (-9.81%), and end-to-end
  latency 738.778→705.759 ms (-4.47%).

### Evidence boundary

- The latest token-envelope result is one warmup plus one measured request. It
  proves semantics and path activation, not statistically strong throughput.
- The current environment has no verified RDMA fabric or second host. TCP,
  SHM, PCIe P2P, and same-host NVLink results are not presented as RDMA or
  dual-node evidence.
- Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen2.5-Omni, and MiniCPM-o require complete repeated GPU
  campaigns; adapter/preflight or CPU transport coverage is not described as
  equivalent real-model performance evidence.
- C4/C16 repeats, 95% confidence intervals, cold/warm/mixed ablations,
  equal-resource colocated replicas, upstream Mooncake PD, and compatible
  SGLang comparisons remain publication gates.

## Latest performance follow-up (2026-07-27, `0e3742e0`)

This update ports a bounded subset of the post-PR performance work onto the
current PR head without replacing the newer PR implementations. The standalone
local development tree remained read-only.

- Added configurable WAL group commit with interval/record thresholds, terminal
  flush, ownership-safe close, and IO counters. Generated EPD deployments use a
  250 ms / 64-record profile; direct control-plane users retain immediate-fsync
  defaults unless they opt in.
- Added a bounded pending-record threshold to connector metrics snapshots while
  preserving the existing interval and request-terminal flush behavior.
- Replaced unlimited Decode HTTP pooling with bounded connections and short-lived
  keepalive. Prefill idle reuse remains disabled by default because retrying an
  ambiguously completed Prefill POST is unsafe.
- Replaced whole-request deepcopy in multimodal URL rewriting with a structural
  copy of only the mutable message/prompt containers; large immutable data-URL
  strings remain shared and the caller request remains unchanged.
- Exported all allocated non-null Prefill KV blocks for P→D handoff, including
  valid hashed prefix-cache blocks, while retaining sliding-window clipping and
  compatibility fallbacks for older vLLM block containers.

Validation for this commit:

- 91 targeted CPU/control-plane/proxy tests passed after the change.
- WAL, registry, and serving-control subsets were rerun independently and passed.
- Python compile and `git diff --check` passed.
- No benchmark artifacts, logs, model paths, or local orchestration state were
  committed.

No new GPU performance claim is made by this commit. A fresh pinned-vLLM 0.23
connector/GPU rerun remains pending because the installed vLLM environments are
0.22.1/0.20.1 and the host NVML interface was unavailable during final push-time
verification. The previously documented real Qwen3-VL evidence is unchanged.

## Motivation

Multimodal and Agent workloads expose reusable state that is not represented
by a conventional colocated request lifecycle:

- Vision Encoder output can be reused across requests and Agent steps.
- Prefill KV cache can be transferred to independently scaled Decode workers.
- Parallel Agent branches can share immutable KV pages and materialize only
  modified pages.
- Thinking, interactive, and hybrid tasks benefit from different Prefill,
  Decode, priority, and latency policies.

Mooncake provides the transport and shared-state foundation needed to make
these states first-class serving objects.

## Task coverage

### Foundation

- [x] vLLM EPD prototype: Vision Hidden State moves from Encoder to Prefill,
  then paged KV cache moves from Prefill to Decode.
- [x] Agent State Cloning: branches share page references with Copy-on-Write
  and explicit lifecycle management.
- [x] Qwen-VL end-to-end demo: real-model launchers, colocated baseline,
  scale-out runner, metrics, and strict direct-path gates.

### Advanced

- [x] Worker-level transfer primitives: registered pointers, peer buffers,
  layer grouping, topology affinity, and transport telemetry.
- [x] Agent PD scheduling: task-type pools, deadline/rho-aware admission,
  backpressure, and affinity-aware dispatch.
- [x] Hidden State Prefix Caching: stable keys, event prefetch, FeatureHandles,
  vLLM hidden-state injection, and Vision Encoder skip.
- [x] Upstream contribution package: public design, evaluation, tests, and a
  proposed reviewable PR split.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Client --> Proxy[EPD Proxy and Scheduler]
    Proxy --> Encoder[Vision Encoder]
    Encoder -->|FeatureHandle and peer buffer| Prefill[vLLM Prefill]
    Prefill -->|Grouped layered KV| Decode[vLLM Decode]
    Decode --> Client

    Proxy <--> Registry[Workflow Registry and WAL]
    Proxy <--> Directory[Owner-sharded KV Directory]
    Registry <--> Agent[Agent Clone and CoW]
    Encoder <--> MMCache[MM Hidden State Cache]
```

See [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md) for interfaces,
lifecycles, data flow, and tradeoffs.

## Main changes

### Mooncake Transfer Engine

- Add registered-pointer batch transfer for persistent KV regions.
- Preserve registration ownership when memory is already registered.
- Improve intra-node CUDA stream dependency handling.
- Expose prepare, write, registration, and bandwidth telemetry.

### Encoder-to-Prefill FeatureHandle

- Add Prefill-owned direct feature buffers with readiness, reference counting,
  bounded persistent cache, and explicit release.
- Add validated FeatureBundle descriptors for Qwen-VL hidden state, DeepStack
  intermediates, and `grid_thw`.
- Add vLLM-side `epd-direct://` materialization and precomputed
  `image_embeds` injection.
- Add event-driven cache prefetch and concurrent request coalescing.

### Prefill-to-Decode layered KV

- Add generation-fenced `KVTransferManifestV2` validation at both producer and
  consumer boundaries.
- Connect grouped layer descriptors to the vLLM producer/consumer save/load
  path.
- Add direct peer-buffer transfer, topology affinity, receive progress, and
  strict transfer counters.
- Preserve handoff identity across prepare, commit, rollback, and release.

### vLLM request path

- Add bounded strict-render reuse with dynamic handoff metadata re-injection.
- Add prompt-only Prefill capability negotiation and exact prompt/MM envelope.
- Add media-free Decode token dispatch with strict identity, placeholder,
  sampling, and KV-generation validation.
- Preserve OpenAI streaming chunks, usage, finish reasons, cancellation, and
  timeout behavior through the compact internal path.

### Agent state and serving control plane

- Add Store-backed page-reference clone, page-level Copy-on-Write, persistent
  catalog/WAL, materialization, connector acknowledgement, and garbage
  collection.
- Add owner-sharded directory state and workflow registry/WAL transitions.
- Add thinking, interactive, and hybrid task routing.
- Add explicit queued/running/first-token lifecycle, telemetry confidence,
  queue/service/transfer cost, deadline, rho, backpressure, and rejection
  metrics.

### Hidden cache and Omni pipeline

- Add exact L1/L2 hidden-state reuse with stable content keys, event
  synchronization, Store manifests, leases, singleflight, and recovery.
- Keep partial prefix reuse capability-gated behind a semantic oracle.
- Add independent-process Omni stage envelopes with real POSIX-SHM descriptor
  and TCP relay transports, cancellation, cleanup, and truthful unsupported
  RDMA/CUDA capability reporting.

### Benchmarks and documentation

- Add real Qwen-VL EPD, colocated baseline, 2P2D scale-out, Agent clone, and
  multi-model evaluation-matrix runners.
- Add fail-closed gates for real services, direct transfer, cache reuse,
  prompt/KV identity, resource scope, output evidence, and lifecycle cleanup.
- Add public `README.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `EVALUATION.md`, submission material,
  and a compact evidence snapshot.

## Compatibility and security

- Existing Mooncake and non-EPD vLLM startup remains unchanged.
- Workspace-scoped vLLM patches are enabled only when generated EPD workers set
  `MOONCAKE_EPD_ENABLE_VLLM_PATCHES=1`.
- Direct FeatureBuffer routes require a generated deployment token through
  `X-Mooncake-EPD-Token`.
- Strict serving confines file-backed FeatureHandles to configured store roots.
- Public interfaces retain existing defaults; EPD behavior is activated by
  explicit launcher and connector configuration.
- TCP is covered by public measurements. A separately staged engine has a
  strict same-host text-only P→D `nvlink_intra` artifact with native worker-log
  evidence; it is not yet an installed-release, full multimodal E→P→D, or
  dual-node result. SHM and RDMA remain capability-gated transport selections;
  the current environment has no verified RDMA fabric or second-node evidence.

## Validation

From the Mooncake repository root:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD

PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
```

title: [Bugfix][Python] Keep async batch IDs opaque with TENT
body:
## Description

With `MC_USE_TENT=1`, Python's `batch_transfer_async_read/write()` writes a timestamp through a classic `Transport::BatchDesc*`, and `get_batch_transfer_status()` reads its task and slice lists. TENT's native batch has a different layout. A two-engine TCP loopback test on main `5e739763f` segfaults while waiting for an ordinary asynchronous WRITE batch.

Keep asynchronous deadlines in the Python wrapper, keyed by opaque batch ID and protected by its existing mutex. Preserve the submission-time deadline (`MC_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT` plus the requested byte count); consume the records when batch waiting takes ownership, and erase single-poll records before freeing a batch so a reused ID cannot lose its new deadline. Completion queries and batch reclamation still use the existing engine APIs.

Add a READ/WRITE regression for multiple outstanding batches, plus single-submit completion coverage. Register it for classic TE and TENT, and run both in the existing CUDA-off CI job, including the necessary path filters.

Refs #3995 (an additional Python compatibility gap). #4143 fixed the analogous Store completion path. #3508 covers deferred reclamation and #2524 covers retry hints; neither fixes these Python batch-layout casts. This PR adds no transport retry, scheduling, or reclamation mechanism.

## Module

- [x] CI/CD

## Type of Change

## How Has This Been Tested?

Built locally on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12, `USE_TENT=ON`, `USE_CUDA=OFF`, `WITH_TE=ON`, `BUILD_UNIT_TESTS=ON`.

```bash
cmake --build build --target engine -j4
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --no-tests=error \
  -R '^(python_async_batch_(classic|tent)_test|tent_python_(send_probe|first_buffer)_test)$'
git diff --check
```

- Baseline main: the original multi-batch READ/WRITE reproducer passes with classic TE; TENT exits with SIGSEGV at `get_batch_transfer_status()`.
- Fixed: all four CTests pass, including data equality after READ and WRITE.
- Upstream [Build & Test (Linux)](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/actions/runs/35321594074) passes on the current documentation head `76509bfd6`, including CI Gate and the CUDA-off TENT job. The classic/TENT async-batch regressions passed in CI; CUDA-enabled runtime tests are skipped. The new CMake test block is formatter-clean.

title: [Bugfix][Store] Make dummy-client TTL configurable and heal stale registrations
body:
## Description

Two independent defects prevent a dummy client from surviving — and then
recovering from — a monitor-driven eviction of its shared-memory segments.

**1. The dummy-client live TTL is hardcoded to 10s.**
`DEFAULT_CLIENT_LIVE_TTL_SEC` (`mooncake-store/include/types.h`) is not
overridable. Any operation that occupies the single-threaded UDS channel for
longer than 10s starves the pings of every other dummy client on that channel,
and `dummy_client_monitor_func` then evicts segments that are still in active
use. In our deployment the blocking operation is pool registration (~20s per
192GB L2 segment); #2198 reports the same failure caused by a 3.5s SSD
`batch_get`; #2937 is a third instance of the same deadline.

This PR makes the TTL overridable via `MC_DUMMY_CLIENT_TTL_SEC`. **The default is
unchanged.** Unset, empty, and invalid values (non-integer, zero, negative,
partially-numeric such as `12abc`) fall back to the default with an error log.
The effective value is logged once at monitor startup so operators can verify the
override took effect.

Note that #2198 proposes raising the default to 60s. We deliberately did not do
that: it would delay detection of genuinely dead clients by 6x for every
deployment, and the right value depends on pool size and storage latency, which
the project cannot know in advance. That decision is left as a separate
follow-up.

**2. After an eviction, the client cannot recover.**
When `RealClient` has no shm context for a client it returned `INVALID_PARAMS`,
indistinguishable from a genuine caller error. The dummy client's
`ShmSegment::registered` flag is a client-side cache of "RealClient has this
segment mapped", kept in sync only by the client's own register/unregister
calls. A monitor eviction unmaps the segment on the RealClient side without
notifying the dummy client, so the flag desyncs: it still reads `true` while the
mapping is gone. That makes the next `register_buffer()` a silent no-op — it
skips the real work (re-sending the fd over UDS so the store re-mmaps and
re-registers the MR) whenever the flag is already `true` — and the client loops
on `shm_not_mapped` indefinitely. This is the symptom reported in #1711.

This PR introduces a dedicated `DUMMY_BUFFER_NOT_MAPPED` error code for the "not
currently mapped in RealClient" case, and the batch entry points
(`batch_put_from`, `batch_get_into`, and both `*_multi_buffers` variants) clear
the stale flag on receiving it. Clearing the flag re-syncs the client-side cache
with the real mapping state, so the next `register_buffer()` performs a real
re-registration: the fd is re-sent over UDS and the store re-mmaps and
re-registers the MR.


`ShmSegment::registered` becomes `std::atomic<bool>` because batch-op threads and
`register_buffer()` callers touch it concurrently. The surrounding check-then-act
sequences are still not atomic as a whole; the remaining interleavings are benign
(a redundant re-registration, which is idempotent server-side, or one extra
failed op before the flag is cleared and healed).

Documentation: `MC_DUMMY_CLIENT_TTL_SEC` is documented under
`### Method C — Resource-owning Real Client` in
`docs/source/deployment/mooncake-store-deployment-guide.md` rather than in the
`### Engine Runtime Tuning (MC_*)` section, because that section states its
variables apply to all deployment methods while this TTL only exists in the
dummy↔real client topology.

### Relationship to existing issues and PRs

- Refs #2198 — implements the "make it configurable" half of that request. Note
  that issue was auto-closed as stale by a bot rather than because the problem
  was addressed; the hardcoded TTL is still present on `main`.
- Refs #2937 — same 10s deadline. Note this PR does **not** address the second
  suspect raised there (`RealClient::ping` returning `UNDEFINED` driving the
  dummy client into a reconnection loop with sparse pings); that is a separate
  defect.
- Refs #1711 — the `shm_not_mapped` loop this recovery path fixes.
- **Differs from #1734 (merged).** #1734 made the offload RPC async to reduce how
  often clients expire, i.e. it lowers the trigger probability. It did not make
  the post-eviction state recoverable. On current `main` the silent-no-op
  re-registration path is still reachable; the added regression test
  `EvictedShmContextRecoversOnNextRegisterBuffer` reproduces it.

## Module

- [ ] Transfer Engine (`mooncake-transfer-engine`)
- [x] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)
- [ ] Mooncake Conductor (`mooncake-conductor`)
- [ ] Reshard (`mooncake-reshard`)

- [ ] Mooncake PG (`mooncake-pg`)
- [ ] Integration (`mooncake-integration`)
- [ ] P2P Store (`mooncake-p2p-store`)
- [ ] Python Wheel (`mooncake-wheel`)
- [ ] Common (`mooncake-common`)
- [ ] Mooncake RL (`mooncake-rl`)
- [ ] CI/CD
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Other

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other

## How Has This Been Tested?

Three tests were added to `mooncake-store/tests/dummy_client_get_buffer_test.cpp`:

- `EvictedShmContextRecoversOnNextRegisterBuffer` — end-to-end reproduction.
  Registers a buffer, unmaps the client's shm context exactly as the monitor does
  on TTL expiry, asserts the batch op reports `DUMMY_BUFFER_NOT_MAPPED`, asserts
  the local `registered` flag was cleared, then asserts that `register_buffer()`
  restores the mapping and the next batch op succeeds. Without the fix the last
  two assertions fail.
- `DummyBufferNotMappedIsADistinctErrorCode` — the new code is distinct from
  `INVALID_PARAMS` and has a `toString` mapping.
- `DummyClientLiveTtlSecHonoursEnvOverride` — default when unset, valid override,
  surrounding-whitespace tolerance, and fallback for `0`, `-5`, `abc`, `12abc`,
  `1.5`. Restores the pre-existing env value on exit.

**Test commands:**
```bash

make -j$(nproc) dummy_client_get_buffer_test

# default run
./mooncake-store/tests/dummy_client_get_buffer_test

# the two checksum cases, which self-skip unless the env var is set
MOONCAKE_STORE_CHECKSUM=1 ./mooncake-store/tests/dummy_client_get_buffer_test \
  --gtest_filter='DummyClientGetBufferTest.GetIntoRejectsCorruptedObjectWithChecksum:DummyClientGetBufferTest.BatchQueryPreservesObjectChecksum'
```

**Test results:**

      with `MOONCAKE_STORE_CHECKSUM=1`)
- [ ] Integration tests pass (if applicable)
- [x] Manual testing done — validated on a two-node PD-disaggregated deployment:
      with the TTL raised, pool registration no longer starves other dummy
      clients' pings into a spurious eviction, and a client whose segments were
      already unmapped recovers on its next `register_buffer()` instead of
      looping on `shm_not_mapped`.

title: [TransferEngine] Add opt-in RDMA MR size override
body:
## Description

On the tested Ionic stack, `ibv_query_device()` advertises a 2 GiB `max_mr_size`, but a single **4 GiB MR backed by 1 GiB HugeTLB pages** registered and completed READ/WRITE operations above the 2 GiB boundary. Mooncake clamps `MC_MAX_MR_SIZE` to the advertised value, so raising that existing variable cannot select the measured larger MR size.

Add an opt-in, classic-RDMA-only registration chunk limit:

```bash
MC_RDMA_MAX_MR_SIZE_OVERRIDE=4294967296
```

Unset preserves today's behavior. A valid override takes precedence over both `MC_MAX_MR_SIZE` and the device clamp for RDMA only; the shared `max_mr_size` remains device-clamped for other transports. Parsing accepts only positive decimal byte counts representable as `size_t`; malformed values are ignored with a warning. The option applies to all selected RDMA NICs and memory registrations in the process, including device memory.

The chunker, pre-touch path and context registration guard use the same effective limit. Larger buffers still split into independently keyed MRs; registration errors propagate and existing rollback remains intact. There is no silent truncation, smaller-MR fallback, or change to transfer slice size. Device initialization logs the advertised and effective limits when overridden.

This extends **#2644 / #2017**, rather than reverting its correctness fix. That PR repaired a mismatch between advertised buffer coverage and the MR actually registered. The override changes the chunk size while preserving its metadata and cleanup behavior.

### Ionic findings and source pointers

Measurements on 2026-09-16 used two MI355X hosts, `ionic_0` on each, host memory backed by 1 GiB HugeTLB pages (`KernelPageSize: 1048576 kB`), and `RDMAV_HUGEPAGES_SAFE=1`. Installed driver: `ionic_rdma 25.08.4.004`; firmware: `1.117.5-a-66`.

| Test | Observation |
|---|---|
| Device capability | `max_mr_size = 2147483648`; `page_size_cap = 0x40201000` |
| Direct libibverbs: one 4 GiB MR on each endpoint | Returned MR length `4294967296`; all 12 READ/WRITE probes passed with exact payload matches |
| Probe positions, each 64 KiB | Offset 0; 2 GiB − 64 KiB; 2 GiB − 32 KiB (straddling); 2 GiB; 3 GiB; 4 GiB − 64 KiB |
| Negative control: same mapping, server registers only 2 GiB | Four in-bounds probes passed; all eight out-of-bounds probes failed. Seven returned remote-access error; straddling READ returned retry-exceeded |
| Existing Mooncake binary, one 4 GiB API registration request | Auto-split into two 2 GiB MRs; all 12 corresponding probes passed with matching SHA-256 |
| Cleanup | Free hugepages restored, zero user MRs/contexts, no new Ionic dmesg lines |

The single-4-GiB-MR result is **direct verbs**, not Mooncake silently creating one MR. The negative control reproduces the coverage error; it is not an unpatched Mooncake build. These experiments motivate the override but are **not a hardware run of this patch**. They do not establish GPU-memory support, a larger universal maximum, a >2 GiB RDMA message, or a performance benefit.

The public driver explains why the advertised value need not describe this hugepage-backed path:

- [`ionic_query_device()`](https://github.com/pensando/dsc-drivers/blob/7d368d059180328edfe0b086d9e0da3beacb7536/drivers/linux/rdma/drv/ionic/ionic_ibdev.c#L75) computes `max_mr_size = npts_per_lif * PAGE_SIZE / 2`, using the kernel base page size. The public source does not document why the factor is exactly one half.
- [`ionic_reg_user_mr()`](https://github.com/pensando/dsc-drivers/blob/7d368d059180328edfe0b086d9e0da3beacb7536/drivers/linux/rdma/drv/ionic/ionic_controlpath.c#L965) preserves the requested length and selects a supported mapping page size using `ib_umem_find_best_pgsz()`. It does not compare the length against that advertised value.
- [`ionic_create_mr_cmd()`](https://github.com/pensando/dsc-drivers/blob/7d368d059180328edfe0b086d9e0da3beacb7536/drivers/linux/rdma/drv/ionic/ionic_controlpath.c#L896) passes the full length as a 64-bit field and separately specifies translation page size.
- [Upstream Linux](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/238650ef6c7c7cca08e032527329424c9fbd70e5/drivers/infiniband/hw/ionic/ionic_ibdev.c#L37) uses the same capability formula. These are pinned public sources, not a verified source match to the installed vendor build.

We deliberately do not infer an automatic larger limit from hugepage size: CPU backing pages do not prove NIC translation granularity or available shared table capacity.

### Mooncake code pointers

- [Existing device clamp](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/blob/ffe013517eaafa8f33e5e0ee034fd6b8f5561e92/mooncake-transfer-engine/src/config.cpp#L835): retained unchanged.
- [Separate override and effective-limit helper](https://github.com/Dao007forever/Mooncake/blob/8e4325a394f61d8e48c4a596aa2c93478d525fbe/mooncake-transfer-engine/include/config.h#L49).
- [Registration chunking](https://github.com/Dao007forever/Mooncake/blob/8e4325a394f61d8e48c4a596aa2c93478d525fbe/mooncake-transfer-engine/src/transport/rdma_transport/rdma_transport.cpp#L303) and [context guard](https://github.com/Dao007forever/Mooncake/blob/8e4325a394f61d8e48c4a596aa2c93478d525fbe/mooncake-transfer-engine/src/transport/rdma_transport/rdma_context.cpp#L630).
- [RDMA Store delegation](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/blob/ffe013517eaafa8f33e5e0ee034fd6b8f5561e92/mooncake-store/src/client_service.cpp#L56): already returns no Store-level registration limit for RDMA; no Store change is needed.

## Module

- [x] Transfer Engine (`mooncake-transfer-engine`)
- [x] Docs

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation update

## How Has This Been Tested?

Linux arm64 CPU build; no RDMA hardware required for the new tests.

```bash
cmake --build <build> --target config_test rdma_mr_override_test rdma_transport_submit_task_test -j 4
ctest --test-dir <build> --output-on-failure \
  -R '^(config_test|rdma_mr_override_test|rdma_transport_submit_task_test)$'
# 100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 3

pre-commit run --files <the nine changed files>
# All applicable hooks passed, including changed-line clang-format 20.1.8.

cd docs && make html
# Build succeeded; new option confirmed in generated HTML.
```

- [x] Unit tests pass: 114 configuration tests, including six new override cases; five new tests exercise the real RDMA registration/chunking paths with mocked verbs; existing transfer-submission regression target also passes.
- [ ] Hardware integration of this patch: not yet run. Prior Ionic measurements above are motivation, not validation of the patched binary.
- Invalid-input tests include zero, negatives, signs, suffixes, whitespace, and overflow. Device-discovery tests verify the override survives successive clamps while the shared limit remains clamped.
- Mocked-verbs tests verify larger registration lengths, separate descriptors/rkeys, unregistering all chunks, error propagation and rollback without smaller retries, the lower-level guard, and pre-touch registration.
