## Description

This PR refactors `peer_client_test` and `p2p_client_integration_test` from in-process integration tests into cross-process integration tests. The resulting topology more closely matches real deployments (client and server / master run in separate processes).

### Background & Motivation

Previously:

- **`peer_client_test`**: The test fixture directly created `TransferEngine`, `TieredBackend`, `coro_rpc_server`, and `ClientRpcService`, then connected `PeerClient` to an RPC port in the same process.
- **`p2p_client_integration_test`**: `InProcP2PMaster` started the P2P master inside the test process, followed by `P2PClientService` instances for registration and read/write operations.

This in-process layout has limitations: the server and client share address space and global state, which does not exercise real RPC/handshake/registration paths and makes it harder to validate cross-machine behavior in the real world.

- Extract shared cross-process test infrastructure into two helper headers (`peer_client_process_test_helper.h`, `p2p_client_process_test_helper.h`) for spawning and managing child processes.
- Run the RPC server (`peer_client_test`) and P2P master (`p2p_client_integration_test`) in separate child processes instead of in the test process; test binaries re-exec themselves via `--mooncake-child-mode` flags.

title: [Bugfix] Register SSD replicas per owner after client restart
body:
## Description

Fix a bug where a **restarted client's SSD (local-disk) replica registration could be silently dropped**, leaving offloaded objects with no disk replica once the old owner is swept.              
                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  When a client crashes and restarts, it comes back with a **new UUID** but the same on-disk files and RPC endpoint. On restart it rescans its SSD objects and re-reports them to the master (via    
  `NotifyOffloadSuccess`, or `AddReplicaForRetainedClient` on the retained-client path). At that moment the **old owner's disk replicas may still be registered**, because owner cleanup happens     
  through the heartbeat/liveness lifecycle rather than immediately.                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Both registration paths deduplicated existing disk replicas by **storage medium** (`Replica::fn_is_local_disk_replica`) — i.e. "does this object already have *any* local-disk replica?". So while 
  the old owner's replica was still present, the new owner's report was treated as already-existing and effectively discarded. Once the old owner was later swept, the object was left with **no disk
  replica at all**, even though the new client had already reported it — forcing another rescan (or a memory-replica fallback) to recover.

### Fix                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Deduplicate by **owner (`client_id`)** instead of by medium, in both paths (`master_service.cpp`):                                                                                                 
  - `AddReplicaForRetainedClient`                                                                                                                                                                    
  - `NotifyOffloadSuccess`                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  A disk replica is now treated as "already registered" only when the **same owner** already has one:                                                                                                
  - Repeated rescan batches from the **same owner** stay idempotent (the descriptor's endpoint/size is refreshed in place).                                                                          
  - Replicas from **different owners coexist** until the old owner is removed by its normal lifecycle cleanup.                                                                                       
  - The restarted owner's registration is no longer lost.                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  A key or RPC endpoint cannot prove that two owners share a disk, so owner identity (`client_id`) is the only safe dedup key.

title: [Store] Add object storage adapter and OSS integration
body:
## Description

This PR ports the Alibaba Cloud OSS implementation from #3008 onto the
object-storage abstraction introduced by #3043 and updates it for the current
`main` branch.

Unlike #3008, this version does not model OSS as a filesystem. It implements
`ObjectStorageAdapter`, so `DistributedStorageBackend` keeps the two storage
models separate:

```text
DistributedStorageBackend
├── FileSystemAdapter       shard / descriptor / offset semantics
└── ObjectStorageAdapter    opaque logical key / whole-object semantics
```

The OSS adapter uses the OSS REST API with V4 HMAC-SHA256 request signing and
supports:

- contiguous and vectored object uploads;
- full and ranged reads;
- existence and size checks;
- object deletion;
- paginated ListObjectsV2 scans; and
- optional end-to-end startup health checks.

Logical Mooncake keys are reversibly encoded under the configured object
prefix. OSS credentials and endpoint settings are read from `MOONCAKE_OSS_*`
environment variables, with the compatibility fallbacks retained from #3008.
The build enables the adapter when libcurl and OpenSSL are available.

The storage factory recognizes `MOONCAKE_DFS_FS_ADAPTER=oss` (with
`MOONCAKE_DISTRIBUTED_FS_TYPE` as the existing fallback). `FileStorage`
selects its control plane from the constructed backend mode: filesystem-backed
distributed storage continues to use DFS, while OSS uses the regular offload
control path.

### Relationship to existing work

- #3008 contains the original provider-specific OSS implementation. This PR
  ports that implementation rather than developing a second OSS client.
- #3043 established the object-storage boundary used here and explicitly
  reserved the OSS provider integration for a follow-up.
- This PR does not change the DFS shard/offset data path or the file-per-key
  storage layout.

### Validation status and open items

The adapter, backend integration, pagination, health-check flow, opaque-key
round trips, and DFS/object-mode selection are covered by local tests. A real
OSS lifecycle test is present but was skipped locally because OSS credentials
are not available in the development environment.

Before marking the PR ready for merge, the provider-specific behavior should
be validated on the exact PR head by the #3008 author or another reviewer with
access to an OSS environment. Review should also confirm the supported encoded
key-length contract, ensure internal health probes cannot appear in `ListKeys`,
and decide whether `CheckHealth` should retain source compatibility through a
default implementation.

title: [Bugfix][Store] Properly enable O_DIRECT for OffsetAllocator vector I/O
body:
## Description

Fixes #3611.

`OffsetAllocatorStorageBackend` passed `use_direct_io=true` to `UringFile` and logged "O_DIRECT mode enabled", but the data file was opened without `O_DIRECT`, and `BatchOffload`/`BatchLoad` use unaligned `vector_write`/`vector_read` iovecs that bypassed direct-I/O alignment handling.

This PR properly enables O_DIRECT end-to-end:

1. Set `O_DIRECT` on the fd when opening OffsetAllocator data files (`Init`, `TryRecoverFromMetadata`, `RemoveAll`) when uring is enabled.
2. Add bounce-buffer alignment handling (with RMW on writes) in `UringFile::vector_read` and `vector_write` so unaligned iovecs work under `use_direct_io=true`.
3. Add `UringVectorIoHandlesUnalignedDirectIo` in `posix_file_test.cpp` to cover unaligned vector I/O under O_DIRECT, including neighbor-data preservation across RMW writes.

Follow-up to maintainer review: the earlier approach of setting `use_direct_io=false` was incorrect; this implements the expected O_DIRECT behavior instead.

title: [Store] Support GPU buffers in NoF reads and writes
body:
Fixes #4128.

## Description

Clients such as vLLM keep KV cache data in GPU buffers, but the NOF path
requires contiguous CPU DMA buffers for SPDK I/O. This PR adds CPU staging
in Store Client to support GPU buffer reads and writes through the NOF
backend.

When a NOF replica is accessed with GPU buffers, the client uses the
existing SPDK DMA pool for staging:

- PUT: Gather GPU slices into a contiguous CPU DMA buffer, then write it
  to NOF.
- GET: Read NOF data into a CPU DMA buffer, then scatter it into the
  destination GPU slices.

Batch operations retain the existing submit-then-wait flow. Batch writes
reuse one staging buffer for all NOF replicas of the same object.
Allocation fails if the staging pool is unavailable or exhausted.

Add a GPU multi-buffer E2E test, a launcher, and usage documentation.

## Module

- [x] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)
- [x] Integration (`mooncake-integration`)

## Type of Change

Successfully built `store` and `mooncake_master` with `USE_CUDA=ON`,
`USE_NOF=ON`, and `USE_TENT=OFF`.

Ran the E2E test with an isolated master and SPDK TCP malloc target:

```bash

SPDK_DIR=/path/to/spdk \
NOF_TEST_PYTHON=/path/to/.venv/bin/python \
bash mooncake-store/tests/e2e/run_nof_gpu_staging_e2e.sh
```

The test passed. It writes non-contiguous GPU slices, verifies that each
object has exactly one NOF replica, overwrites the source buffers, and
reads into separate GPU buffers. After CUDA synchronization, both the
payload and untouched buffer gaps match the expected values.

title: [Store] Add bounded batch OpLog deletion primitive
body:
## Description

Add `OpLogBatchStorage::DeleteBatchesThrough(batch_id)` for N10 of the batch OpLog retention work tracked in #3167 and #3808. The operation deletes records through the inclusive cutoff within one cluster's batch-record namespace, preserving later batches, durable prefix, producer view, snapshot control keys, and other clusters.

Reuse the existing fixed-width batch range helper, including its `UINT64_MAX` boundary, and expose bounded deletion through `HaKvBackend` and `EtcdHaKvBackend`. Empty existing ranges and repeated deletes succeed; errors propagate without widening the range or retrying in storage. The etcd adapter rejects empty, unbounded, and reversed bounds.

This PR has no production deletion caller. The future N12 coordinator must validate the cutoff and publish a reader-visible compaction floor before invoking it. N09 reader rebootstrap landed in #4048; #4049 separately handles snapshot object GC, rather than batch-record deletion. Legacy snapshot implementation is untouched.

title: [Store] Avoid replica descriptor copies in batch writes
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #4085. That PR removed redundant replica descriptor copies from
read paths; this change removes the analogous copies when adopting master
responses in batch write paths.

### Problem

`Client::StartBatchPut` and `Client::StartBatchUpsert` receive one vector of
`Replica::Descriptor` objects per key from the master. The successful response
entry is not used after the corresponding `PutOperation` is initialized, but
the previous code copied the complete vector into `op.replicas`.

Each descriptor can contain dynamically allocated endpoint and path strings.
Consequently, every successful key in a batch write paid for a vector copy and
copies of all descriptor strings. The same copy also occurred when the
dangling local-disk replica retry path recovered an operation.

### When it happens

This is normal production behavior for successful `BatchPut` and
`BatchUpsert` requests. The cost grows with batch size and replica count, and
is especially visible when descriptors contain non-SSO endpoints or paths.

### Solution

Move the response vector into `PutOperation::replicas` at the three ownership
transfer points. The response entries are not read after assignment, so this
preserves all descriptor values while transferring the existing vector buffer
without allocating or copying its elements.

### What is not changed

- Replica ordering, allocation accounting, transfer submission, and error
  handling are unchanged.
- The master RPC, wire format, and public client interfaces are unchanged.
- The moved-from response entries are not used after assignment.

## Performance evaluation

A standalone benchmark uses the repository's `Replica::Descriptor` and
`tl::expected` types. It converts 30,000 successful keys with one, two, or
three memory replicas per key. Endpoint strings are deliberately longer than
the small-string optimization threshold. Values below are medians of 10 runs;
all times are in milliseconds and allocations cover only the
response-adoption loop.

| Memory replicas per key | Before (ms) | After (ms) | Time reduction | Before allocations | After allocations |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3.166 | 0.097 | 96.9% | 60,000 | 0 |
| 2 | 5.992 | 0.101 | 98.3% | 90,000 | 0 |
| 3 | 8.569 | 0.103 | 98.8% | 120,000 | 0 |

The benchmark isolates local metadata adoption rather than claiming an
end-to-end RPC latency improvement. It measures the exact copy-versus-move
operation removed by this change.

## Correctness evaluation

The differential benchmark compared vector size, replica ID and status,
transport endpoint, protocol, buffer address, and size for 128 keys with three
memory replicas each. The result was equivalent.

| Test | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Differential copy/move descriptor comparison | Equivalent |
| `client_integration_test` default mode | 21 passed, 4 checksum tests skipped by configuration |
| Checksum-enabled integration tests | 4/4 passed |
| `pybind_client_test` batch put/upsert tests | 3/3 passed |
| Dangling local-disk replica recovery test | Passed |

title: [Bugfix][TENT] Detect dead peers in CheckSegmentStatus under MC_USE_TENT
body:
## Description

Under MC_USE_TENT the classic shim's CheckSegmentStatus() returned Status::OK() unconditionally. The Python wrapper (transferSync / batchTransferSync) only evicts a cached peer handle from handle_map_ when that status is non-OK, so a dead peer's handle stayed cached forever and every retry reused the same stale segment.

Delegate to TENT's probePeerAliveByID(), which fails on a stale/unknown handle (invalid handle), an empty RPC address, or an unreachable peer (RPC error), and map any non-OK result to Status::Endpoint so classic callers close and re-open the segment.

The eviction path also called engine_->getMetadata()->removeSegmentDesc(), but getMetadata() returns nullptr under TENT (same root cause as the send_probe crash). Now that the branch is reachable, null-guard it: TENT invalidates its own segment cache inside closeSegment(), so the classic metadata cleanup is skipped when there is no classic metadata object.

Adds TransferEngineTentCompatibilityTest.CheckSegmentStatusRejectsDeadPeer, which fails on main (blind OK) and passes after the fix.

Refs #3995 (P0-stale-handle)

title: [Store] Tenant-first object-level metadata locking (flat group)
body:
## Description

Implements **object-level metadata locking** for the Mooncake Store (issue #3670, flat-group model from #3589).

Today a single coarse **shard lock** serializes all writes and eviction on a shard, so unrelated objects contend on one lock. This PR replaces it with a **per-object lock** (`ObjectEntry::mutex`) plus a **per-tenant object route**: an object is excluded only while it is itself being read, written, or evicted. Group semantics keep the routing decoupling of #3589 in a thinner form — a group is a membership table plus one shared `Lease` (`GroupIndex`), consulted only by eviction for all-or-none decisions; the read path never touches the group table.

New modules under `mooncake-store/include/tenant/`:

- `MetadataCatalog` — boundary between MasterService and the tenant module; owns the tenant registry and lifecycle rules.
- `TenantDirectory` — copy-on-write `TenantId` → `TenantCatalog` map; lock-free reads, atomic get-or-create.
- `TenantCatalog` — per-tenant aggregate: quota handle, `ObjectIndex`, `GroupIndex`.
- `ObjectIndex` — flat key → `shared_ptr<ObjectEntry>` route with identity-checked erase (`EraseIf`), publication generations for remove/recreate races, and the dynamic-replication lease table.
- `ObjectEntry` — per-object mutex guarding the metadata envelope and all per-key task state that previously lived in parallel shard maps.
- `ObjectMetadata` / `object_replica_list.h` — extracted metadata envelope (identity, replicas, lease, soft-pin, quota ledger).

Concurrency rules: route locks are never held together with object locks (strong handles bridge the gap), teardown is claimed once per entry (`is_torn_down`), and a route slot is erased only against the exact entry being torn down, so a concurrent remove + re-create cannot drop a live object.

**Performance A/B** (Debug builds, same machine and compiler, same workload). baseline = pre-PR master (`ca09c18d`, shard locks), this PR = `7960b555`. 2x4GiB segments, 1MiB values, fixed arrival, groups of 5 consecutive put keys share one group_id, eviction driven to the 0.8 high-watermark on both.

Metadata plane (client→master RPC, `master_synthetic_bench`), 60s per run:

| workload | ref | p50 (ms) | p99 (ms) | p999 (ms) | item_qps | rpc_fail |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| medium | baseline | 1.608 | 58.68 | 104.10 | 2173.7 | 148 |
| medium | **this PR** | **1.595** | **8.87** | **10.79** | 2173.7 | 148 |
| high | baseline | 1.743 | 61.39 | 106.95 | 4347.5 | 390 |
| high | **this PR** | **1.503** | **8.63** | **10.95** | 4347.5 | 390 |

p99 -84.9% / -85.9%, p999 -89.6% / -89.8%; p50 -0.8% / -13.7%. `rpc_failure_events` align on both sides (148 vs 148, 390 vs 390) and item_qps are identical, so the comparison is same-load. The shard-lock baseline tail is also unstable across runs (medium p99 varied 58-79 ms between rounds); this PR stays in a 9-13 ms band.

**Isolation under churn.** One client writes 1MiB objects at full speed to keep eviction continuously active; a second client runs a mixed read/write workload against the same master. Victim p99: baseline 52.9 → 85.9 ms under churn; this PR 28.6 → 46.4 ms. Under churn, this PR's victim tail stays below even the baseline's uncontended p99 (46.4 vs 52.9 ms).

**2x load, 16 workers** (metadata plane, fixed arrival at ~8695 item/s on both): baseline p99 105.5 ms, this PR 12.4 ms; `rpc_failure_events` identical (876 both). This PR's p99 stays in the 9-13 ms band from 1x to 2x load.

**Memory cost.** Master RSS measured over a 90s linear small-object write (~1M objects): baseline ~0.8 KB/object, this PR ~1.2 KB/object (+~0.4 KB, about +50%). The increase is the per-object lock, generation and task state folded into `ObjectEntry`, plus the route key stored next to `ObjectMetadata::user_key` — roughly 4 GB of master RSS at 10M objects. This is the cost of the per-object locking model; compaction (single key storage, on-demand task allocation) is left as follow-up work.

End-to-end runs (`store_kv_bench`, real data movement through the transfer engine, eviction continuously active) show the same direction: throughput 1800 → 2788 MiB/s and p99 52.9 → 28.6 ms. title: [TransferEngine] Report Redis error replies as failures in the metadata plugin
body:
## Description

Fixes #4099. `RedisStoragePlugin::set()`/`remove()` treated any non-null reply as success and never inspected `reply->type`, so a `REDIS_REPLY_ERROR` — the server deliberately rejecting the write — was reported to `registerSegmentDesc()` as a completed publish. The likely trigger is a failover: a promoted replica, or a load balancer briefly routing to one, answers `-READONLY`, which is a valid reply object, so the write was dropped with no signal anywhere. `-OOM` at maxmemory, `-MISCONF` and `-NOAUTH` take the same silent path.

`set()`/`remove()`/`get()` now check `REDIS_REPLY_ERROR` and log the server's error string, so `-READONLY` is distinguishable from a connection failure. `getWithStatus()` maps it to `kUnavailable` directly instead of letting the error text reach the JSON parser as a misleading parse error. The check mirrors the AUTH/SELECT handling already in the same class.

No retry is added on purpose: the server answered, so the command was received and rejected; only the reporting was wrong.

## Module

- [x] Transfer Engine (`mooncake-transfer-engine`)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## How Has This Been Tested?

There is no existing test harness for this plugin, so I built one off-tree for this PR: the current `RedisStoragePlugin` class is extracted verbatim into a test driver at build time (so the binary runs the actual PR text, not a copy), linked against the real hiredis, and driven against a minimal fake Redis server speaking RESP2 that answers `-READONLY` to every write.

**Test commands:**
```bash
# fake Redis answering -READONLY to every command, then driver with the plugin under test
python3 fake_redis.py <port> error &   # modes: error / ok / miss
./driver <port> error
```

**Test results:**
- Stock (unpatched) class on `-READONLY`: `set()=true, remove()=true` — the silent write loss, reproduced.
- Patched class on `-READONLY`: `set()=false, remove()=false, get()=false`, `getWithStatus()=kUnavailable`, and the log carries the server's error string (`READONLY You can't write against a read only replica.`).
- Patched class on normal replies: `set()/remove()/get()` succeed, `getWithStatus()=kFound` — no behavior change on the healthy path.
- Patched class on a nil GET: `getWithStatus()=kNotFound` preserved — authoritative absence still distinguishes from outage, as `syncSegmentCache` relies on.

title: [TENT] Align Ascend Direct with async AutoConnect-only transfer
body:
## Description

Aligns TENT Ascend Direct with classic TE **behavior** (async + AutoConnect, plus same-engine local copy). Tracking RFC: https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/3919

Rebased onto current `main` (includes #4027). Store still creates TENT through classic `TransferEngine::init()`, so the `globalConfig()` → TENT Config copy in `transfer_engine.cpp` stays until Store constructs `tent::TransferEngine` natively.

RFC #3919 originally left same-engine ACL memcpy out of scope (use `TransferAsync` even for self). HIXL rejects connection-with-self, so this PR adds a **per-NPU** `LocalCopyEngine` instead of process-wide classic TE `LocalCopyEngine` / `MC_STORE_MEMCPY`.

What this PR changes:

- Split the transport into a facade (`AscendDirectTransport`) plus one `HixlEngine` per NPU. Vendor HIXL is behind `HixlEngine::Vendor` so unit tests inject a fake (there is no `HixlClient` type).
- Cross-engine datapath is `TransferAsync` + poll only: no `TransferSync`, no `Connect()`, no `BufferPool`. `Initialize` always sets `AutoConnect=1`. Default `LocalCommRes` is `{"version":"1.3"}` (`ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES` may override).
- Same-engine copies use that engine’s `LocalCopyEngine` (`aclrtMemcpyAsync` + D2H host flag). Stream/context are created and used under that NPU’s ACL context (`ContextGuard`); this is not the process-wide stream that [classic TE #3993](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/3993) hit.
- Each HIXL engine gets a dataplane `listen_port` distinct from its TCP name. RoCE `listen_port` is injected only in `roce_mode`.
- Classic TE shim in `TransferEngine::init()` copies Store/dummy-real flags from `globalConfig()` into TENT Config (`agent_mode` / `store_te_init` / `fabric_mem`) under `MC_USE_TENT=1`.
- When `MC_TENT_CONF` is a file, `loadFromEnv()` replaces the whole Config. Those nested keys are restored via the existing constructor whitelist. **`tent/common/config.h` is unchanged.**
- `getLocalIpAndPort()` returns the advertised TENT segment name when set.
- Topology maps location type `"npu"` to `MEM_ASCEND`. Default `transfer-engine.json` grows an `ascend_direct` block (`enable: true`).
- Mock-HIXL unit tests (`tent_ascend_direct_transport_test`, 24 cases).

title: [PG] Fix P2P epoch matching and destroy/reinit test ordering
body:
## Description

Related CI runs:

- [CI run 34685683490 Attempt 1](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/actions/runs/34685683490/attempts/1?pr=4060)
- [CI run 34685683490 Attempt 2](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/actions/runs/34685683490/attempts/2?pr=4060)

This PR resolves two issues in `mooncake-pg` that led to occasional CI failures:
1. P2P epoch matching inconsistency across view updates.
2. A race condition in `test_destroy_and_reinit`.

### P2P Epoch Matching Issue

Previously, `mooncake-pg` validated incoming credits/ACKs against the current group epoch. Consequently, a membership view update triggered by an unrelated rank bumped the group epoch, causing in-flight P2P operations across uninvolved ranks to fail.

This PR shifts the epoch validation baseline to the epoch at the moment the receiver enqueues the operation:
- The sender adopts this initial epoch, requires all subsequent credits for the transfer to match it, and echoes this epoch in every ACK.
- The sender also uses the group epoch at reset time as a lower bound for credit epochs issued by the receiver.

This confines the impact of a view update strictly to the ranks directly involved in the membership change.

> **Note:** This fix is limited to preserving credit/ACK matching across view updates while the corresponding P2P lane is not reset -- i.e., resets on unrelated ranks will no longer disrupt healthy in-flight P2P operations.
>
> Guaranteeing deterministic, reproducible ordering for P2P/collective operations across rank rejoin boundaries requires a more robust global quiescing phase to prevent races between view updates and in-flight operations. This also involves synchronization with captured work during replay, which is out of scope for this PR and will be addressed in follow-up PRs or under #3483.

### Ordering Issue in `destroy_and_reinit`

In the current test, a "fast" rank could finish `destroy_group()` and immediately invoke `init_process_group()` before other ranks have finished destroying their instances. Under this condition, the coordinator still finds a matching group and rejoins the fast rank as an inactive member -- violating the test's intent of having all ranks cleanly tear down and reconstruct a brand-new group.

This race cannot simply be resolved via internal synchronization inside PG. Consider the following timeline:
- Ranks 0–3 concurrently run `destroy` and `init`.
- Rank 0 finishes `destroy` ahead of ranks 1–3 and starts initializing a new group.
- When the coordinator receives Rank 0's request, it cannot distinguish between:
  1. A replacement rank registering after an old rank's graceful leave.
  2. The test's intended scenario where Rank 0 is creating an entirely new group in-place.

The ambiguity exists because PyTorch reuses `group_id`s (`bootstrap_id` in Coordinator). The coordinator relies on this PyTorch-provided ID and the policy specified during rank initialization (`CreateOrAttach` vs. `ExtendOrAttach`, corresponding to `is_extension = false` and `true`). When the PyTorch group ID matches an existing group and the policy permits attaching, the coordinator naturally chooses to attach/rejoin the existing group in-place.

Differentiating these cases inside PG would require tracking group generations in one process or introducing additional user flags. This would add unwanted complexity and restrict flexibility (e.g., preventing a process from legitimately destroying a group and re-initializing to rejoin an existing one without a process restart).

Therefore, this PR addresses the issue by introducing a barrier between group destruction and re-initialization.

title: [Store] Shrink metadata maps after ClearStaleHandles sweeps
body:
## Description

### Background

`std::unordered_map::erase` never returns bucket-array memory — a container that once held millions of entries keeps its high-water bucket array after mass erases (8 bytes/bucket × tens of millions of buckets), so RSS is not released. #3576 introduced `ShrinkBucketsIfSparse` to address this, rehashing a container down via `rehash(size*2)` when its bucket count exceeds 1024 and its load factor drops below 25%.

However, #3576 only invoked it at the end of `BatchEvict` (marking evicted shards with an `evicted_shards` bitset), **missing the `ClearStaleHandles` path, which can also delete keys at a large scale**.

### Observed Symptom

When multiple store nodes share a tenant and one node goes offline:

- The master-side key count keeps dropping as the SSD is unloaded (tens of millions of keys), but **RSS does not drop**;
- When that node recovers and starts writing again, both the key count and RSS **continue to climb further**.

### Root Cause

A store node goes offline → `client_monitor` flags it `BECAME_OFFLINE` → enqueues a `ClientOffboardingJob` → `UnmountSegment` → `ClearInvalidHandles` → `ClearStaleHandles`. This function erases key metadata held by the offline node in per-shard batches via `EraseMetadata`, but at the end it only erases empty tenants — **it never calls `ShrinkBucketsIfSparse`**.

Because multiple stores share the tenant, the offline node only deletes its own subset of keys, so the tenant stays non-empty → the `metadata` map keeps its high-water bucket array → RSS is not released. When the node recovers and writes again, the map grows on top of the high-water baseline → RSS climbs further.

### Fix

Add a shrink pass at the end of `ClearStaleHandles`' shard loop, mirroring the one in `BatchEvict`:

- Introduce a `bool erased_in_shard` flag, set after each of the two synchronous `EraseMetadata` call sites;
- After the shard is fully processed (including the empty_tenants cleanup), if `erased_in_shard` is true, take the write lock and call `ShrinkBucketsIfSparse(metadata)` for each **still-live** tenant.

The write lock is only taken for shards that actually had erasures; `ShrinkBucketsIfSparse` is O(1) — two comparisons and an early return when the map is not sparse — so the overhead is negligible. A fully emptied tenant is already destroyed by `shard->tenants.erase` (its inner map is released along with it), so it neither needs nor can be shrunk — this fix precisely targets the "partially drained" shared tenant.

### Known Limitation

Under the `enable_ha_ && enable_oplog_` path, the actual `EraseMetadata` is deferred to the durable-finalize callback `FinalizeMetadataEraseAfterDurable` and does not occur inside `ClearStaleHandles`, so it is not covered here. The synchronous path (non-HA, or HA without oplog) is covered. Shrinking on the HA path must be added separately in the finalize callback and is left as future work.

**New regression test:**
- `ClearStaleHandlesShrinksSparseMetadataMaps`: reproduces the production scenario of "multiple stores sharing a tenant + partial drain". Two segments share the default tenant; the stale segment holds ~1920 keys to be deleted, while the live segment holds 128 surviving keys to keep the tenant from being erased entirely. Keys are filtered onto a single shard so the `metadata.bucket_count()` crosses the `kShrinkMinBucketCount` shrink threshold; after `PauseReplicaCleanup`, `UnmountSegment(stale)` + `ClearInvalidHandlesForTest` deterministically trigger the sweep. Assertions: `buckets_after < buckets_before / 2` (without the shrink the bucket array stays at its high-water mark and this fails), `buckets_after >= live_keys.size()` (the shrunk map still holds every surviving key), `GetKeyCount() == live_keys.size()` (physical metadata is actually deleted, not merely hidden), and live keys are queryable while stale keys return `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`.

title: [Bugfix][TransferEngine] Honor retry hints in RDMA request preselection
body:
`TransferEnginePy::transferSync()` assigns its outer retry index to
`TransferRequest::advise_retry_cnt`. The classic RDMA request-wide fast path,
however, calls `Topology::selectDevice()` without that hint. A whole-buffer
retry can therefore select the retry-zero preferred HCA again and bypass the
per-slice path that already honors the hint.

Forward `request.advise_retry_cnt` into the existing request-wide selector.
Hint zero remains the default, so first-attempt routing is unchanged. Requests
that cannot be selected as a whole continue through the existing per-slice
fallback.

This is complementary to #2524: that PR advances hints in the batch wrapper;
this two-file slice makes the classic RDMA request-wide consumer observe the
hint. Related: #2960 and #3696.

title: [Bugfix][TENT] Forward classic RDMA device filters
body:
## Description
Refs #3995 (P0-device-filter).

When existing callers run through the classic Transfer Engine compatibility layer with MC_USE_TENT=1, the RDMA device filter passed to the classic API is currently dropped:


Python initialize(device_name)
  -> buildDeviceFilter()
  -> TransferEngine(auto_discover, filter)
  -> TENT compatibility path drops filter
  -> TENT discovers and initializes every local HCA
For example, calling:


engine.initialize(..., device_name="mlx5_bond_0")
on a host with four HCAs still causes TENT to discover and initialize all four devices.

This PR forwards the caller-provided filter into TENT's existing RDMA whitelist configuration:


Python initialize(device_name)
  -> buildDeviceFilter()
  -> classic TransferEngine constructor
  -> tent_device_filter_
  -> buildTentConfig()
  -> topology/rdma_whitelist
  -> platform probe filters discovered HCAs
  -> only the requested RDMA contexts are initialized

title: [TE] Fix double-free in freeBatchID under CONFIG_USE_BATCH_DESC_SET
body:
## Summary
- `batch_desc_set_` stores `shared_ptr<BatchDesc>`, but `freeBatchID()` did `delete &batch_desc` followed by `batch_desc_set_.erase(batch_id)`. The erase triggers the `shared_ptr` destructor, which deletes the already-freed object — double-free.
- Fix: under `CONFIG_USE_BATCH_DESC_SET`, let the `shared_ptr` own the lifetime (erase only); without the flag, keep the manual `delete` (no `shared_ptr` involved).
- Fixed in both `MultiTransport::freeBatchID` and `Transport::freeBatchID`.

## What was NOT changed
- `allocateBatchID` is unchanged
- Non-`CONFIG_USE_BATCH_DESC_SET` paths are unchanged
- No changes to batch lifecycle or API

## Test plan
- [ ] CI build (both with and without CONFIG_USE_BATCH_DESC_SET)
- [ ] Code review: `#ifdef`/`#else` makes the two ownership models mutually exclusive

title: [TENT] Validate sub-batch type in getTransferStatus
body:
## Summary

`getTransferStatus` is a public Transport API, but five transports dereferenced the result of `dynamic_cast<XxxSubBatch*>(batch)` without a null check: TCP, SHM, MNNVL, NVLink, and io_uring. SunriseLink's `getTransferStatus`, RDMA's `cancelTransferTask`, and (since #3280) GDS already validate — this PR applies the same guard to the remaining five for a uniform error surface.

The internal poll path is type-safe (`pollTaskStatus` indexes transport and sub-batch by the same `task.type`), so this is API hardening/consistency, not a reachable crash on current main.

Also adds a mismatch regression test (`TcpTransportSubBatchTest.RejectsForeignSubBatchInGetTransferStatus`, per review): hands an ShmSubBatch to TcpTransport (and the reverse) asserting InvalidArgument, plus a matching-type case. CPU-only, no install() required.

> Rebased on latest main: the GDS hunk from the original version was dropped — #3280 added an equivalent check upstream. `rdma_transport.cpp` remains out of scope (being reworked in #3016).

## Test plan

- [x] Regression test discriminates: reverting the guards makes it dereference nullptr
- [x] CI (all transports; tent-ci cuda-on/off)
